jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
**EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR JOB DESCRIPTION**

**Location:** Los Angeles, CA

**Job Type:** Full\-Time, hybrid

**About LocoL**

Alta Community (dba LocoL) is a nonprofit in Watts, which provides culinary job training and education for young people while addressing food insecurity through the preparation and distribution of affordable, high\-quality meals, primarily for local nonprofits. Founded as a nonprofit in 2023 by chefs Keith Corbin and Daniel Patterson, LocoL is on the site of the former LocoL restaurant, originally founded by chefs Roy Choi and Daniel Patterson.

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director reports to the Board of Directors and has overall authority and accountability for organizational strategy, personnel, operations, programs, fundraising, and financial management, within policies and budgets approved by the Board.

The Executive Director will lead Alta Community/LocoL through its next stage of organizational development, strengthening the systems, partnerships, revenue, team, and strategy required to deliver sustainable community impact. The Executive Director will have overall responsibility for organizational leadership, fundraising and earned\-revenue growth, financial stewardship, program quality and impact, team development, and external relationships.

This is an opportunity for a hands\-on, entrepreneurial leader who can move comfortably between long\-term strategy and practical execution. The successful candidate will understand how to build an emerging nonprofit organization while respecting LocoL’s history, community relationships, culinary identity, and commitment to economic opportunity and food justice.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Leadership, Strategy \& Administration**

* In partnership with the board of directors, develop and execute a strategic plan for the next five years of growth and impact.
* Ensure operational and programmatic alignment with the organization’s values and goals.
* Engage the Board through quarterly meetings to facilitate effective org governance.
* Improve and implement HR practices for employee success, including performance management, compensation and staffing, and employee development and retention.
* Build and develop a high\-performing, inclusive team, ensuring role clarity and fostering a culture of growth, accountability, and teamwork.
* Ensure compliance with California employment requirements.

**Fundraising, Communications \& Financial Management**

* Develop and implement a revenue strategy including earned income meal contracts, grants, and individual giving to raise and sustainably expand \~$700K operating budget.
* Build and maintain relationships with donors, foundations, and funding partners.
* Strengthen partnerships with nonprofits, community leaders and hiring partners.
* Leverage data to enhance organizational storytelling and external communications to grow awareness, convey impact to key stakeholders, and drive fundraising targets.
* Oversee financial planning, budgeting, and resource allocation for fiscal sustainability, including cash\-flow management, financial controls, monthly financial reporting and forecasting, grant reporting, insurance and risk management and earned income margins.
* Ensure compliance with all appropriate tax and accounting standards, as well as nonprofit regulations, reporting, and best practices.
* Oversee planning of fundraising and community events, as needed.

**Program Development**

Recruit and manage a new Program Manager to ensure organizational alignment and effective program delivery. Program Manager responsibilities include:

* Manage six program staff members and develop a hiring plan to fill additional capacity needs within the organization.
* Expand and refine programs that provide culinary training, cooking education, and affordable catering for nonprofits.
* Ensure operational success for LocoL, including kitchen operations, quality control, menu development, budgets, vendor relationships and customer service.
* Collaborate with chef leaders at LocoL to develop and implement a job training program, focusing on culinary skills, hospitality, and professional development.
* Mentor and coach team members, many of whom are entering the workforce for the first time, to help them achieve their full potential.
* Oversee outcome measurement to demonstrate effectiveness.

**Required capabilities**

* Passion for community and workforce development, food justice, and economic empowerment.
* Proven executive or senior leadership in nonprofit management, social enterprises, or related fields.
* Experience partnering with board of directors and leading teams.
* Strong track record in fundraising, grants, and financial management.
* Excellent strategic thinking, communication, storytelling, and advocacy skills.

**Strongly preferred capabilities**

* Social\-enterprise leadership.
* Food, culinary, hospitality, catering, or production experience.
* Los Angeles or Watts community relationships.
* Early\-stage organizational building.
* Brand and communications experience.
* Government contracting or institutional meal contracts.

**Compensation \& Benefits**

* Salary Range: $90,000\-$110,000 (commensurate with experience).
* Stipend for healthcare.
* Paid\-time off and paid sick time.

**How to Apply**

Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter to **info@altacommunityla.org** with the subject line **“Executive Director Application – LocoL.”** Priority will be given to applications received by August 31, 2026\.

Pay: $90,000\.00 \- $110,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Paid time off

People with a criminal record are encouraged to apply

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Los Angeles, CA 90002

**JOB DESCRIPTION**  

  

  

We are looking for a Senior MLOps engineer to work closely with Data Scientists to build and deploy ML models on a modern MLOps stack.
As an Executive Director Machine Learning Engineer on the Recommendation Engine team, you'll implement fine\-tuning and reinforcement learning algorithms on large compute clusters, build and run real\-time and batch model serving systems, hyper\-parameter tuning at scale, model monitoring, production validation and other activities vital for model development, testing and deployment in a well\-managed, controlled environment.
Our product, Personalization and Insights, builds and supports high throughput, low latency applications which leverage state of the art machine learning architectures, and which are deployed in AWS. These applications power personalized experiences across Chase Consumer \& Community Banking channels, to help weave a user experience that includes traditional banking services with other services in the Travel, Merchant Offer Shopping, and Dining spaces.
Job responsibilities
* Build, deploy, and maintain robust pipelines for distributed training on GPU\-enabled clusters to support scalable machine learning workflows.
* Develop and manage high\-volume real\-time and batch inference systems, ensuring optimal performance and reliability.
* Implement quantization techniques and deploy open\-weight large language models (LLMs) on modern serving stacks such as vLLM on Ray to maximize efficiency and resource utilization.
* Oversee the management and optimization of vector databases to support advanced AI and machine learning applications.
* Establish and maintain comprehensive monitoring and observability pipelines to ensure system health, performance, and rapid issue resolution.
* Collaborate with cross\-functional teams to integrate new technologies and continuously improve existing infrastructure.
* Partner with product, architecture, and other engineering teams to define scalable and performant technical solutions.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills
* BS in Computer Science or related Engineering field with 10\+ years of experience Or MS degree in Computer Science or related Engineering field with 6\+ years experience.
* Solid knowledge and extensive experience in Python or in cloud computing and AWS.
* Understanding of quantization techniques such as PTQ, AWQ etc. used to quantize LLMs for accelerating inference on specific GPU architectures
* Solid understanding of Transformer models and challenges involved in serving large transformer\-based models
* Solid understanding of ML training, especially latest reinforcement learning algorithms such as GRPO and DAPO
* Experience in systems engineering fundamentals: caching, CUDA, autoscaling, high throughput, low latency, x\-region resilient applications
* Deep knowledge and passion for data science fundamentals, training and deploying models
* Experience in monitoring and observability tools to monitor model input/output and features stats
* Solid grounding in engineering fundamentals and analytical mindset

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills
* Experience with recommendation and personalization systems is a plus.
* CUDA experience is a big plus
* Solid fundamentals and experience in containers (docker ecosystem), container orchestration systems \[Kubernetes, ECS]
* Experience with Ray, vLLM, RL libraries such as verl/trl
* Good knowledge of Databases

**Position Summary**

### The Director of Development is Project Hospitality's senior fundraising leader responsible for implementing and managing a comprehensive fundraising program that expands philanthropic revenue, strengthens donor relationships, and supports the organization's long\-term financial sustainability. Reporting directly to the Chief Advancement Officer (CAO), the Director of Development serves as a key member of the Advancement leadership team and is responsible for executing fundraising strategies aligned with Project Hospitality's mission, strategic priorities, and organizational goals.

### The Director of Development provides leadership for day\-to\-day fundraising operations, including major gifts, annual giving, foundation and corporate partnerships, donor stewardship, fundraising campaigns, signature events, and community engagement. Working closely with the Chief Advancement Officer, the Director of Development cultivates and stewards donor relationships, identifies new funding opportunities, and ensures the successful execution of the organization's advancement initiatives.

### The Director of Development collaborates with the Senior Development Associate and other assigned development staff such as advancement consultants, grant writers, and external fundraising partners as directed by the Chief Advancement Officer. The Director ensures that departmental activities, systems, and resources are aligned to achieve fundraising goals and support organizational growth.

### In partnership with the Chief Advancement Officer, the Director of Development supports the work of the Board of Directors' Development Committee by preparing reports, coordinating meetings, and assisting with Board engagement in fundraising and donor cultivation activities.

* Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree preferred.

* Experience managing fundraising campaigns, donor stewardship, and development operations.
* Experience supervising staff and managing multiple fundraising initiatives.
* Excellent interpersonal, written, verbal, and presentation skills.

**Preferred**

* Experience in human services, healthcare, or a mission\-driven nonprofit organization.

The salary range for this position is **$80,000\-$85,000**, commensurate with qualifications and experience. The Cornerstone program is offered every weekday from 9:00 am to 10:00 pm, Saturdays from 10:00 am to 5:00pm, and extended hours during the summer and school holidays. jobs.title: Full-Time Program Director at Cornerstone - Brooklyn, NY
jobs.description:
**Cornerstone Director**


Founded in 1981, NIA Community Services Network is a nonprofit organization dedicated to addressing issues that impact youth, families, and seniors. NIA’s mission, to strengthen and empower children, families, and communities through comprehensive programming and vital human services, is evidenced each day through services that directly support and enrich the lives of children and families we serve at more than 50 program sites located across many of New York City's most diverse and underserved neighborhoods through after\-school programs, summer day camps, cultural arts opportunities, youth and family counseling services, parent workshops, community assistance, referral services, senior support programs, and community events.


Visit us at www.niabklyn.org.


Cornerstone Programs, funded by the NYC Dept. of Youth and Community Development (DYCD), are located in NYCHA community centers throughout New York City and provide academic and recreational opportunities for children, teens, and adults. NIA is seeking a Cornerstone Director to manage a community center located in Coney Island, Brooklyn. The center offers services every weekday from 10:00am to 10:00pm, Saturdays from 10:00am to 5:00pm. The center operates on school holidays and is open for extended hours in the summer from 8:00am through 11:00pm, 7 days a week.


The Cornerstone Director is the lead on\-site supervisor of the Cornerstone program, responsible for managing day\-to\-day operations of the site, including staff supervision, facility management, scheduling and programming, administrative tasks, and stakeholder relationships. The position of Cornerstone Director is a critical, visible position requiring exceptional leadership, strong management experience, and a successful track record of working with government contracts and nonprofit organizations providing social services. The Director should be highly flexible in dealing with the challenges of program management and working to meet the needs of the community with compassion and innovation. The Director should have experience with community\-based services for youth, children, and/or families.




The Director should have proven ability to manage staff professionally and interact with the community using a strengths\-based approach. They must be a hands\-on strategic thinker, a planner and problem solver. Excellent communication skills are critical. The Director must be comfortable communicating with participants from the community, and equally comfortable in communicating with staff, organization leadership, funders, and community officials.

**Responsibilities:*** Effectively manage on\-site staff, including assistant directors, community liaison, direct\-service Group Leaders and Instructors, security team, and building maintenance team.

Founded on the conviction that art should be accessible to everyone, the Frye has served as a welcoming gathering place for nearly 75 years—where artists, audiences, ideas, and communities come together through meaningful, unique encounters with modern and contemporary art.

  



The museum is known not only for the quality of its exhibitions and programs centered on the art of our time, but also for its culture of experimentation, curiosity, generosity, and creative joy. Internally, we believe our best work emerges through collaboration across disciplines and departments. Externally, we partner closely with artists, educators, civic leaders, cultural organizations, and community members to imagine new possibilities for what an art museum can do and be in Seattle.

  



As the Frye approaches its 75th anniversary, the museum is entering an ambitious period of institutional growth. Building on a strong financial foundation and a clear strategic vision, we are investing in new earned revenue initiatives, technology, campus improvements, and organizational capacity to ensure the museum remains a vibrant public resource for generations to come.

  



The next Chief Financial \& Operating Officer will play a central role in helping realize that vision.

The Frye seeks a strategic, entrepreneurial Chief Financial \& Operating Officer to serve as the chief steward of the museum’s business and operational enterprise, which together represent a total organizational budget of just under $12 million annually and assets valued at approximately $166 million.

The CFO/COO serves as a member of the Executive Team and provides strategic leadership for the museum's enterprise functions, including:

* Facilities, capital projects, and real estate
* Security and public safety operations
* Retail, café, and other earned revenue initiatives

Success in this role depends less on personally being the technical expert in every operational discipline than on building excellent teams, aligning leaders around shared priorities, and creating and integrating systems that enable the museum and its teams to perform at a high level.

**About Lantern Residences**

Lantern Residences provides structured, recovery\-focused housing for adult men rebuilding their lives following substance\-use treatment, incarceration, homelessness, or other periods of instability.

Our approach is built around stability, structure, dignity, accountability, and long\-term progress. We believe that no one heals without a home and that accountability should never require humiliation.

We are seeking an experienced and highly organized **Program Director** to lead the daily operation of our recovery residences, supervise program staff, maintain compliance, strengthen resident outcomes, and ensure consistent standards across all locations.

**Position Summary**

The Program Director is responsible for the overall quality, consistency, safety, and operational performance of Lantern Residences.

This is a hands\-on leadership position for someone who can supervise multiple staff members and properties while managing resident concerns, documentation, compliance, performance expectations, referral relationships, and operational priorities.

The ideal candidate is comfortable making decisions, holding staff accountable, responding calmly to difficult situations, and creating systems that ensure important responsibilities do not fall through the cracks.

* Supervise and support house managers, peer\-support staff, case management staff, intake staff, interns, and house leads.
* Lead regular administrative, staff, and house\-lead meetings.

* Review staff performance, communication logs, shift notes, and employee compliance scorecards.
* Provide coaching, corrective action, and performance\-improvement support when expectations are not met.
* Ensure appropriate on\-call and backup escalation coverage.
* Help maintain a professional culture based on structure, dignity, consistency, and accountability.

**Resident Services and Program Oversight**

* Monitor resident progress, behavioral concerns, grievances, return\-to\-use situations, rule violations, and higher\-level\-care recommendations.
* Ensure resident service plans, phase requirements, meeting participation, and case\-management responsibilities are being completed.
* Review overnight incidents, safety concerns, sensitive resident situations, and staff escalations.
* Ensure residents are treated fairly and consistently across all locations.
* Support Housing First conflict\-resolution practices while protecting resident, staff, and community safety.
* Review intakes, discharges, discharge outcomes, and resident progression through the program.
* Ensure urgent court, probation, parole, and referral\-partner communications are handled accurately and promptly.

**Documentation and Quality Assurance**

* Review daily staff shift notes and communication logs across all residences.
* Ensure incidents, grievances, return\-to\-use events, corrective actions, and resident concerns are properly documented.
* Conduct weekly documentation reviews and monthly resident\-chart audits.
* Ensure resident files, service plans, releases, assessments, and program records are complete and current.
* Maintain high documentation standards within BehaveHealth or the organization’s designated electronic record system.
* Reinforce the expectation that undocumented work is considered incomplete.

**Compliance and Accreditation**

* Maintain compliance with Lantern Residences policies, procedures, grants, contracts, and applicable recovery\-housing standards.
* Maintain readiness for South Carolina Alliance for Recovery Residences inspections and other external reviews.
* Conduct recurring compliance audits and assign corrective actions when deficiencies are identified.
* Monitor staff certifications and required training, including CPR, Narcan, financial literacy, and program\-specific training.
* Review medication\-assisted treatment documentation and coordination requirements.
* Support annual policy reviews and continued program improvement.
* Ensure physical locations meet safety expectations, including fire extinguishers, smoke detectors, carbon\-monoxide detectors, emergency exits, and general property safety.

**Operational and Financial Oversight**

* Monitor occupancy, admissions, discharges, resident participation, and program\-performance indicators.
* Review the intake and referral pipeline to ensure applications and partner communications continue moving.
* Review resident accounts receivable and program\-fee follow\-up with case\-management staff.
* Monitor key performance indicators and prepare weekly leadership reports.
* Support monthly financial, grant\-performance, and quality\-assurance reporting.
* Review access\-control systems and ensure access codes match the current resident census.
* Coordinate facilities, maintenance, cleanliness, supply, and property\-related concerns across all residences.
* Identify recurring operational problems and implement sustainable solutions.

**Community and Referral Partnerships**

* Maintain professional relationships with treatment providers, hospitals, jails, courts, probation and parole offices, veterans’ organizations, nonprofits, and other referral partners.
* Ensure communication with referral partners is timely, respectful, and properly documented.
* Monitor referral sources, conversion rates, community events, and partnership performance.

jobs.description:
**Executive Director Rural Health Institute of New York**

**REPORTS TO** Board of Directors

**CLASSIFICATION** Full\-time, exempt

**LOCATION** Cortland, New York, with regional travel

**About RHI**

Cortland Area Communities That Care Coalition, Inc., doing business as the Rural Health Institute of New York (RHI), is a nonprofit public health institute serving rural and underserved communities. RHI turns data into action through epidemiology and evaluation, collaborative leadership and grant administration, health communication, and community systems improvement. Its portfolio includes substance use prevention, mental health and suicide prevention, housing and homelessness, harm reduction, environmental health, early childhood development, and other emerging public health priorities.

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director is RHI's chief executive officer and is accountable to the Board of Directors for mission impact, strategy, organizational health, and responsible stewardship. The Executive Director leads a multidisciplinary team and a complex portfolio of federal, state, local, philanthropic, and contracted initiatives. This leader must pair entrepreneurial vision with disciplined execution, build trust across sectors, and ensure that RHI remains financially resilient, compliant, responsive, and focused on measurable community benefit.

**Essential Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership and Board Governance**

● Develop and execute RHI's strategic direction with the Board, translating priorities into clear annual goals, operating plans, performance measures, and resource decisions.

● Keep the Board fully informed through timely financial, program, risk, and organizational reporting; support strong governance, policy development, committee work, and leadership succession.

● Anticipate shifts in rural health needs, public policy, funding, and partner capacity; position RHI to respond to emerging opportunities without losing strategic focus.

**Organizational Leadership**

● Build an inclusive, collaborative, and accountable workplace where staff understand expectations, receive meaningful supervision, and have opportunities to grow.

● Lead workforce planning, organizational design, recruitment, compensation, performance management, professional development, and succession in partnership with designated staff and the Board.

● Supervise and coach senior leaders, establish clear decision rights, and strengthen systems that support cross\-program coordination, staff well\-being, and consistent execution.

**Financial Management, Resource Development, and Grant Administration**

● Develop and manage the annual budget, cash\-flow plan, forecasts, reserves, and financial dashboards; provide the Board with accurate information for timely decisions.

● Maintain strong internal controls and oversee accounting, audit or financial review, procurement, insurance, contracting, time and effort documentation, and fiscal policies.

● Direct the full grant and contract lifecycle, including opportunity selection, proposal development, budgeting, negotiation, implementation, invoicing, reporting, closeout, and funder compliance.

● Diversify revenue through public and private grants, service contracts, partnerships, philanthropy, and mission\-aligned earned\-income opportunities.

**Program Strategy, Quality, and Learning**

● Ensure programs are evidence\-informed, community\-responsive, contractually sound, and aligned with RHI's mission and core capabilities.

● Connect epidemiology, evaluation, implementation, and health communication so that data consistently informs strategy, messaging, improvement, and investment.

● Establish outcome and process measures, review dashboards and feedback, address performance concerns, and promote continuous quality improvement across the portfolio.

**Partnerships, Public Leadership, and Communications**

● Serve as RHI's principal ambassador and spokesperson, clearly communicating the organization's mission, value, results, and positions to diverse audiences.

● Cultivate durable relationships with residents, community\-based organizations, healthcare systems, schools, counties, funders, government agencies, colleges, and regional or national networks.

● Convene cross\-sector partners, navigate competing interests, negotiate agreements, and represent RHI in public forums while protecting its credibility and independence.

**Operations, Compliance, and Risk Management**

● Ensure compliance with nonprofit, employment, grant, contract, privacy, records, and data stewardship requirements, as well as Board\-approved policies and applicable law.

● Oversee technology, facilities, information security, vendor relationships, business continuity, and other infrastructure needed for safe and effective operations.

● Identify material financial, legal, operational, reputational, and program risks; implement corrective action and promptly elevate significant concerns to the Board.

**Qualifications**

jobs.description:
* Looking to use your fundraising expertise to create lasting impact?
* Passionate about building meaningful relationships that strengthen communities?
* Ready to lead advancement efforts for an organization changing the lives of youth and families?

**Join DFYF's team that is inspiring hope, strengthening families, and restoring our communities!**
**Who we are:**
Directions for Youth \& Families (DFYF) is a nonprofit organization providing community\-based mental health and prevention services through a resiliency\-oriented and trauma\-informed framework. Our programs are organized into three service areas: Treatment, Prevention, and Education. From specialized mental health counseling and kindergarten readiness to afterschool and summer programming, we provide innovative services that meet the diverse needs of youth and families throughout our community.
Each year, DFYF proudly serves more than 8,500 youth, adults, and families fulfilling our mission to build and inspire hope, healing, and resilience for youth, families, and communities through counseling and education.

As our Senior Director of Advancement, you'll play a vital leadership role in expanding the resources and partnerships that make our mission possible. By cultivating donors, strengthening community relationships, and leading strategic fundraising initiatives, you'll help ensure that thousands of children and families continue to receive needed services.
We believe that investing in our employees is essential to fulfilling our mission. That's why we offer a comprehensive benefits package, including free healthcare with $0 deductibles, generous paid time off, 10 paid holidays, retirement benefits, professional development opportunities, and a collaborative, mission\-driven culture where your leadership and impact are valued every day.

**Job Purpose**

The Office of Hawaiian Affairs (OHA) works to improve the wellbeing of Native Hawaiians through advocacy, research, community engagement, land management and the funding of community programs.

The Administrator functions as the Chief Executive Officer ("CEO") of the Office of Hawaiian Affairs ("OHA") and is responsible for implementing and executing the will of the elected Board of Trustees (BOT). Reporting directly to the BOT, the Administrator \& CEO provides executive oversight, strategic \& operational leadership, and oversees organizational performance. The Administrator \& CEO implements Board policy and advances OHA's constitutional and statutory responsibilities on behalf of Native Hawaiian beneficiaries.

The Administrator \& CEO plays a central role in advancing this mission by ensuring that OHA’s people, programs, resources, and partnerships are aligned to achieve measurable results. The Administrator \& CEO maintains stewardship of the strategic planning process, ensuring alignment between Board direction, organizational priorities, operational execution, and performance outcomes.

As the principal executive of the OHA, this role serves as the conduit between the BOT, community, and administrative staff and is responsible for effective communication, leadership and direction. Additionally, the Administrator \& CEO works with other agencies, public and private, that also serve Hawaiians and Native Hawaiians consistent with OHA's mission of bettering the conditions of all Hawaiians.

**Essential Responsibilities**

**Trustee Relations**

Establishes succession strategies, leadership development programs, and knowledge transfer practices to ensure organizational continuity, preserve institutional knowledge, and maintain operational excellence.

* Manages relationships to create optimal opportunities and moves the organization forward.

**Position Summary**

The CEO serves as the strategic leader of MAEDA (aka “Choose Marshall”), a unified

chamber of commerce and economic development organization dedicated to advancing the

prosperity, vitality, and identity of the greater Marshall region. This executive provides vision,

direction, and leadership across all organizational functions — including economic

development, business services, tourism, marketing, events, community engagement,

administration, and partnership building — ensuring high impact for residents, visitors,

businesses, and public\-sector partners.

In addition, the CEO plays a critical role as lead coordinator and relationship manager for

the State of Michigan’s Major Campus industrial development site and associated regional

development initiatives. This includes guiding complex land\-development processes,

coordinating governmental and regulatory actions, navigating infrastructure planning, and

facilitating multi\-agency partnerships to advance one of Michigan’s most significant

transformational economic development opportunities.

**Organizational Overview**

MAEDA leads consolidated economic development efforts for the City of Marshall and

affiliated local development authorities, while also serving as the city’s chamber of

commerce and destination marketing agency. Its mission spans business attraction and

retention, workforce development, tourism promotion, placemaking, downtown vitality,

community storytelling, and major community events.

**1\. Vision, Strategy \& Organizational Direction**

vitality, tourism expansion, and business climate enhancement.

Champion innovation in economic development, marketing, public storytelling, placemaking,

Coordinate infrastructure discussions involving water/sewer systems, utilities,

transportation, and long\-term service planning.

Direct strategies for business attraction, retention, workforce capacity building, and

stewardship of transformational development assets—including the MAJOR Campus.

Michigan’s economic development platforms and grant opportunities.

Guide downtown development, business district enhancement, and beautification programs

hospitality partnerships.

Champion placemaking, historic narrative development, and visitor experience

enhancements that boost regional identity and visitation.

Coordinate planning and implementation related to utilities, transportation, and other

infrastructure essential to development readiness and long\-term community prosperity.

Identify and pursue grant funding, public\-private partnerships, and strategic investments

supporting economic and community development.

**8\. Executive Leadership, Administration \& Organizational Stewardship**

Inspire and lead a multidisciplinary team across economic development, chamber

operations, marketing, tourism, events, and administration.

Oversee financial management, budgeting, reporting, audits, and operational policies.

Foster a high\-performance internal culture built on creativity, accountability, collaboration,

and results.

Prepare reports, presentations, and briefing materials for government bodies, boards, and

stakeholders.

Hire, supervise, develop, and evaluate staff consistent with Board\-approved policies.

We are a small, mission\-driven team, and every staff member plays a direct role in how well we serve our patients, families, and community partners.

We're looking for a tech\-savvy, highly organized Executive Assistant to work directly alongside the Executive Director and become a key partner in modernizing how our organization runs. We welcome candidates at any career stage: recent graduates in healthcare administration or nonprofit/business management, and experienced professionals looking for a meaningful next chapter. What matters most is a genuine desire to make a direct impact on hospice care in our local North Hawaii community.

* Prepare and update letterhead, templates, and other branded materials
* Coordinate building maintenance needs and vendor scheduling

* Cultivate relationships with patient families and recurring donors

* Research and support board development initiatives

**Marketing \& Communications**

* Support marketing coordination and materials using tools such as Canva and AI\-assisted content tools
* Help maintain consistent branding across all communications

* Prepare educational materials for RN Liaisons
* Research and schedule opportunities to speak and educate the community
* Track outreach activities and referrals to measure outcomes

jobs.title: Director of Communications Strategy
jobs.description:
Description:
**About Locus:**


At Locus, we know communities thrive when they have equitable access to capital. We collaborate with stakeholders across the community development ecosystem to invest in communities with strong aspirations, while addressing challenges like a shortage of affordable housing, limited access to fresh food, a lack of quality jobs, and clean energy innovation. We believe a capital system that centers community input and impact is essential to ensure that everyone, no matter their background, location, or economic status, can live in healthy, thriving places.


Locus is the parent organization for a family of community development enterprises, which includes a nonprofit CDFI loan fund, a CDFI bank, a fund management practice, and a national guarantee program. With offices in Christiansburg and Richmond, Virginia, Locus offers innovative and flexible financing tools and strategic consulting services to individuals and organizations in underestimated and excluded communities, most of which are low\-to\-moderate income. Alongside our many partners, Locus has generated over $2 billion dollars in total impact.


Locus is a nonprofit holding company regulated by the Federal Reserve. Locus Bank is an FDIC\-insured, certified bank and B Corp offering products tailored to socially conscious investors. Locus Bank is a majority\-owned subsidiary of Locus. Member FDIC. Equal Housing Lender. Learn more at www.locusimpact.org.

**Position Overview:**


The **Director of Communications Strategy** will report to the Chief External Affairs Officer and work closely with the CEO and other senior leaders to translate Locus’s strategy, impact, and point of view into clear, compelling communications. The role will also support internal communications, select events, and cross\-functional initiatives requiring strong messaging, careful stakeholder management, and disciplined execution. This is a hands\-on role for an experienced communications professional who is equally comfortable developing strategy, writing executive\-ready content, preparing a leader for a high\-stakes engagement, and coordinating the details required to deliver effectively.

**Essential Duties \& Responsibilities:**

**External Communications and Reputation:**

* Develop and execute external communications strategies that advance Locus’s mission, business priorities, reputation, and stakeholder relationships.
* Translate organizational strategy, products, partnerships, impact, and market insights into clear narratives for external audiences.
* Own and maintain Locus’s website content, ensuring it is current, accurate, accessible, and aligned with organizational messaging.
* Manage Locus’s social media strategy and channels, including content planning, publishing, engagement, and performance monitoring.
* Ensure alignment of Locus brand, marketing and communications strategies with Locus mission, vision, values and strategic goals.
* Steward of Locus Brand
* Draft and edit press releases, statements, talking points, opinion pieces, articles, presentations, briefing materials, stakeholder communications, and other public\-facing content.
* Identify opportunities to strengthen Locus’s visibility and position its leaders as credible voices on community finance, economic development, banking, public policy, and related issues.
* Support media engagement, including developing story angles, preparing spokespeople, responding to inquiries, and coordinating with external partners as needed.
* Monitor relevant news, policy developments, public conversations, and reputational issues and recommend communications responses.
* Support issues and crisis communications, including rapid message development, stakeholder coordination, and executive preparation.

**CEO and Executive Communications:**

* Serve as a trusted communications partner to the CEO and other senior leaders.
* Draft speeches, remarks, presentations, opinion pieces, letters, external emails, social content, and other executive communications.
* Prepare concise briefing materials for interviews, panels, conferences, government meetings, partner conversations, and other external engagements.
* Develop talking points, anticipated questions, audience context, stakeholder background, and recommended messages for high\-priority meetings.
* Help maintain a consistent executive voice while adapting messages appropriately for different audiences and settings.
* Work with the CEO and leadership team to identify themes and opportunities for thought leadership.

**Government Affairs and Stakeholder Communications:**

* Support communications related to government affairs, public policy, elected officials, regulators, public agencies, and other civic stakeholders.
* Develop briefing materials, policy\-oriented talking points, letters, testimony, meeting preparation, and follow\-up communications.
* Coordinate with internal subject\-matter experts and external government affairs partners to ensure messaging is accurate, timely, and aligned with organizational priorities.
* Help maintain a clear view of priority government and external stakeholders, relevant issues, and upcoming engagement opportunities.
* Support coalition, association, and partner communications when Locus is participating in a broader policy or advocacy effort.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.description:
**Three generations. Multiple plants. One operator to run them.**


Press\-Seal Corporation has been manufacturing specialty rubber sealing products for the waterworks and industrial markets for three generations, family\-owned throughout. Our products sit underground in municipal infrastructure across North America, where failure is not an option and quality is not negotiable.


We are no longer a single\-plant company. Through acquisition and organic growth, we now operate multiple manufacturing facilities across Indiana, with more expected. We are creating the role of Chief Operating Officer to run them. Ownership will still be involved in plant\-level duties.

**Purpose of Position**


Reporting directly to the CEO, the COO owns manufacturing across all Press\-Seal facilities — Fort Wayne, Jasper, InSeal, and the plants we acquire next. You will carry the operating P\&L and be measured on three things above all: throughput, cost, and margin.


You will also own all of engineering — new product development and plant\-level industrial engineering both. That means one person is accountable for what we decide to build, how fast it gets to launch, and whether the process on the floor can actually make it at cost. Few operating roles at this size carry that whole span.


This is a floor role, not a corner office. You will know the extrusion lines, presses, mixers, lathe\-cut cells, and the people running them. You will decide which work belongs at which plant, where the constraints are, and what capital is worth spending. When we buy a company, you are the one who makes the operating thesis real.

**What You’ll Own**

* Consolidated operating P\&L across all manufacturing sites
* All engineering — new product development and plant\-level industrial engineering
* Plant leadership development and accountability
* Capacity, capital planning, and constraint removal
* Quality systems (ISO 9001, IATF 16949, PPAP, NSF 61\) and EHS performance
* Materials strategy, inventory, and supply resilience
* Operating integration of acquired facilities

**What We’re Looking For**

* A decade or more of manufacturing leadership with multi\-site P\&L ownership — you have run more than one plant at the same time
* Experience leading engineering on both sides: product development timelines and plant\-level industrial engineering
* A track record integrating acquisitions or turning around underperforming operations
* Materials\-processing background: rubber, polymer, plastics, or similar — mixing, molding, or extrusion
* Real fluency in lean methods and formal quality systems
* A results record you can put numbers to


Rubber compounding or molding depth, and experience in waterworks, filtration, or tier automotive supply, will move you to the top of the list.

**Why Press\-Seal**


We are family\-owned and intend to stay that way. That means decisions get made in days, not quarters, and the person setting strategy is in the building. It also means we take a long view — we are building an operating platform, not dressing up a company for sale.


You will report to the CEO with a direct line, a real mandate, and the authority to match it.

Unless explicitly authorized by law, selection will be made without regard to, and there will be no discrimination because of, color, race, religion, national origin, marital status, parental status, physical or mental disability, genetic information, age (40 or over), sex (including pregnancy and related conditions, gender identity, and sexual orientation), or on the basis of personal favoritism, or any other non\-merit factors.

jobs.title: General Psychiatry Residency Program Director - Psychiatrist
jobs.description:
**Description**


**MaineHealth Behavioral Health (MHBH)** is seeking a full\-time (1\.0 FTE) board\-certified Psychiatrist to join the Department of Psychiatry at MaineHealth Maine Medical Center Portland (MHMMCP). This role offers a unique hybrid opportunity, combining leadership and clinical practice.


The selected candidate will serve as the **General Psychiatry Residency Program Director** (0\.5 FTE) while also providing psychiatric clinical care (0\.5 FTE). This position supports a diverse patient population across both rural and urban communities.


This is an excellent opportunity for a psychiatrist interested in academic leadership, with potential for future involvement in additional academic and/or administrative roles.


The MHMMC General Psychiatry residency program combines the intellectual and physical resources of an academic teaching hospital with the patient base and public health commitment of a large community hospital and community mental health center. In addition to the General Adult Psychiatry Training Track, our residency program offers a General Psychiatry/Child \& Adolescent Psychiatry Integrated Training Track, as well as a Rural Psychiatry Training Track. Our care continuum and psychiatry residency training sites also include MaineHealth Behavioral Health at Spring Harbor (a free\-standing 100\-bed psychiatric hospital) and MaineHealth Behavioral Health, a region\-wide comprehensive mental health organization. MHMMCP also includes the Barbara Bush Children’s Hospital, the state’s only pediatric tertiary care center and only Level 1 Trauma Center.


MHMMC has an academic affiliation with Tufts University School of Medicine and offers the best aspects of patient care and academic stimulation. Residents are involved in teaching medical students from Tufts and from the nearby University of New England. Residents are also actively involved in department governance and decision\-making, participating in department retreats and quality improvement projects, and having formal representation on departmental committees.


We are very interested in furthering the practice of psychiatry in New England \- particularly in Maine. We have special options for rural psychiatry rotations while offering community\-based training experiences in Portland. We are proud of our program and take great pleasure in the success of our graduating residents.


MHMMC is a nationally recognized academic medical center with an impressive history of outstanding and innovative residency and fellowship programs. MHMMC is approved to train over 400 trainees in our 17 ACGME\-accredited residency programs, 19 ACGME\-accredited fellowship programs, two rural tracks and rural concentration. We have a culture of continuous quality improvement and our performance in the areas of safety, quality, and satisfaction are consistently excellent. Physicians are expected to apply for faculty appointment to the Tufts University School of Medicine.


The Program Director has full responsibility, authority, and accountability for program administration and operations; teaching and scholarly activity; resident recruitment and selection; evaluation, promotion, and discipline; supervision; and faculty development. The Program Director is charged with developing and maintaining a training plan aligned with ACGME Common and Program\-Specific Requirements and ensuring that all aspects of the program meet accreditation standards. There are robust opportunities to grow and develop teaching experiences and work with both residents and medical students.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Graduate of Allopathic or Osteopathic Medical School. Completion of internship and psychiatric residency and/or fellowship training
* Current or eligible licensure as a physician by the Maine Board of Licensure in Medicine
* Current certification in Psychiatry by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN) or by the American Osteopathic Board of Neurology and Psychiatry
* Current DEA Registration Certificate
* Psychiatry specialty expertise and at least three years of documented educational and/or administrative experience

**This position offers:**

* Competitive compensation package including sign\-on bonus, relocation assistance, CME expense reimbursement, and malpractice insurance.
* Benefits include Paid Time Off, CME time, retirement with employer match, medical, dental, vision, life/disability insurance, paid family leave, wellness program, and more.

**Portland, Maine**: Maine’s largest metro, Portland lies two hours north of Boston. Home to more than 525,000 people, Portland is Maine’s most celebrated city. Forbes.com has ranked it among its Top Ten Most Livable Cities and GQ.com called it One of the Coolest Small Cities in America. Ideal for families and young professionals, Portland offers exceptional foods, lifestyles, and activities. Attractions include its historic Old Port district, craft microbreweries, the Portland Museum of Art, Victoria Mansion, Wadsworth\-Longfellow House and six classic lighthouses. Neighborhoods are welcoming, with many beautiful homes. Public and private schools are excellent. Transportation is reliable, and there are many four\-season outdoor activities to enjoy, from sailing and kayaking to hiking, mountain biking and snowshoeing to skiing at one of 14 Maine\-area ski resorts.

**MaineHealth Behavioral Health (MHBH),** a MaineHealth member, is Northern New England's leading integrated behavioral healthcare system. It serves predominantly southern, western, central and Mid\-Coast Maine, and is composed of southern Maine's only nonprofit psychiatric hospital, outpatient treatment, crisis services, as well as 5 ACT teams. This fully integrated and growing system of behavioral healthcare makes it a regional and national model for treating people with serious mental health issues.

jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement
jobs.description:
**POSITION: Director of Community Engagement and Academy Giving**

**LOCATION: Great Hearts Irving Lower and Upper Schools; Irving, Texas**

**DIRECTLY REPORTS TO: Headmasters of Great Hearts Irving**

**FUNCTIONAL REPORTING TO: GHTX Development**

**SALARY: $50,000\-59,000**

* Occasional travel within Texas may be required.

**About Great Hearts Texas:**


Great Hearts Texas is a network of tuition\-free public schools dedicated to improving education in Texas. A Great Hearts Texas Academy cultivates great\-hearted leaders capable of success throughout their higher education and professional careers. With a curriculum built upon a classical liberal arts tradition and a revolutionary approach to education, Great Hearts Texas nurtures the hearts and minds of students in the pursuit of Truth, Goodness, and Beauty.

**Purpose:**


This role sits at the intersection of development and community relations. The Director of Community Engagement and Academy Giving (DCE) advances the academy’s mission by securing financial support through the annual Community Investment campaign and other giving opportunities, expanding outreach when necessary, and strengthening community ties. Reporting to the campus Headmaster, with functional support from GHTX Development as well as Marketing and Enrollment teams, the DCE plans and executes annual Community Investment campaigns, cultivates donor relationships, and fosters partnerships to boost student enrollment and enhance the academy’s reputation. This role requires strong communication, relationship\-building, and organizational skills. The DCE regularly collaborates with faculty, parents, volunteers, and the broader community to align fundraising priorities with the academy’s mission and effectively expand the academy’s brand and outreach.

**Responsibilities:**

**Fundraising and Development:**

* Lead the planning and execution of the Community Investment campaign in alignment with GHTX strategies to meet and exceed goals.
* Cultivate, solicit, and steward relationships with academy families, faculty, alumni, and community stakeholders to secure financial support.
* Identify and cultivate matching gifts, partnerships, and small grant opportunities toward the Community Investment fund and other fundraising initiatives.
* Using approved platforms, maintain standard operating procedures for gift entry and constituent data records.
* Maintain Community Investment visibility at events, meetings, and other vital channels to foster a culture of philanthropy.
* Report on key metrics and trends to the academy headmasters.
* Attend regular meetings with other Directors of Community Engagement and Academy Giving and central office support teams.

**Community Engagement and Outreach:**

* Advance outreach and marketing impact through strategic efforts to increase brand awareness and enrollment demand according to the academy’s goals.
* Drive initiatives to build strong partnerships by assisting the administration in hosting events, family tours, and other programming.
* Manage or support campus communication channels as needed (email, social, website, etc).
* Serve as a key partner to the academy’s Academy Advisory Committee (AAC) and Parent Service Organization (PSO).
* Represent the academy at internal and external functions, maintaining a positive public image.
* Collaborate with GHTX Marketing and Enrollment teams to promote growth and re\-enrollment.

**Qualifications:**

**Education:** A Bachelor's Degree

**Experience:** Minimum of 2–3 years of successful experience in fundraising, sales, marketing, or a related field.

**Skills:**

* Excellent oral and written communication skills, including presentation and storytelling abilities.
* Strong interpersonal skills with an outgoing, relationship\-oriented personality.
* Proven ability to take initiative, prioritize tasks, and work independently while collaborating effectively with a team.
* Proficiency in data analysis and reporting to inform strategic decisions.
* Experience in enrollment marketing and community outreach is highly desirable.
* Commitment to Great Hearts Texas's mission and classical education principles.
* Fluency in Spanish is an asset.
* Certified Fund\-Raising Executive (CFRE) designation is an asset.

**Computer Skills:**

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).
* Familiarity with Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Slides).
* Experience with constituent databases and giving platforms; familiarity with Raiser's Edge and Classy is beneficial.
* Skilled in utilizing email marketing tools and managing social media outlets.

**Travel Requirements:**


May need to travel locally to meet with academy families, attend school activities, and participate in community events.

**Physical Requirements:**


Ability to perform tasks involving standing, sitting, bending, squatting, reaching, and occasional lifting of up to 15 pounds.


It may require moving or positioning equipment for events and activities.

**Additional Information:**


Must pass a mandatory background screening.


Expected to follow the campus administrative schedule, including participation in summer and winter activities as required.


Serve as a visible and active presence on campus, aligning with the culture and values of Great Hearts Texas.

**Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a criminal history background check and fingerprint clearance in accordance with state requirements.**

**Travel required: May need to travel locally for training and professional development opportunities.**

**This description reflects management’s assignment of essential functions. It does not exclude or restrict the tasks that may be assigned.**

**Great Hearts Academies is an Equal Opportunity Employer.**

**Job Title** Chair and Executive Director \- Associate or Professor in Social Work
  

**Requisition Number** FE04968

**Required Education**
* An earned doctorate in Social Work from an accredited institution
* An earned Master of Social Work degree from a CSWE\-accredited program


  

**Required Related Experience**
A record of teaching, scholarship, and service commensurate with appointment at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor with tenure. Strong potential for securing external funding and producing high\-quality scholarship. Ability to foster, develop, and/or maintain positive professional relationships with local, state, federal, and private social work focused agencies/organizations/associations.
  

**Required License/Registration/Certification**
n/a
  

**Job Summary**
THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY, COLLEGE OF SOCIAL WORK (CoSW) is a renowned leader in higher education. Our mission is clear: Through rigorous research, excellence in instruction, and steadfast service, the CoSW works to improve the human condition. Always, in all ways.  

As the state’s flagship university, CoSW is committed to actualizing our mission through innovative, accessible academic programming. CoSW is home to several undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral programs, including: Bachelor of Arts in Criminal Justice (traditional and online), Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice (traditional and online), Bachelor of Arts in Social Work (traditional and online), Master of Science in Criminal Justice (online), Master of Social Work (hybrid and online), Doctorate of Social Work (online), Ph.D. in Social Work (traditional), and multiple certificate programs. In addition to Lexington’s main campus, we have a satellite campus at Fort Sam Houston in San Antonio, Texas.  

The Chair and Executive Director of Social Work Programs serves as the chief academic and administrative leader for the College’s social work educational enterprise. The Chair provides visionary leadership and strategic oversight for all aspects of the College’s social work programs, including the Bachelor of Arts in Social Work, Master of Social Work, Doctorate of Social Work, Doctor of Philosophy in Social Work, and related certificate programs.  

Reporting directly to the Dean and serving as a member of the College leadership team, the Chair and Executive Director advances the College’s strategic vision through academic leadership, faculty development, student success, community engagement, operational excellence, and organizational growth.  

Primary responsibilities of this position include but are not limited to:  

**Leads Strategic Growth and Innovation*** Develops and implements the strategic vision for the College’s social work programs.
* Guides academic innovation and program growth across modalities.
* Uses workforce, enrollment, and market data to inform planning.
* Identifies opportunities for new educational initiatives.

**Advances Faculty Success*** Recruits, mentors, supervises, and evaluates faculty and instructional personnel.
* Supports promotion, tenure, annual review, and workload planning.
* Supports faculty leadership development.
* Cultivates a collaborative faculty culture.

**Promotes Academic Excellence*** Oversees BASW, MSW, DSW, PhD, and certificate programs.
* Supports curriculum innovation.
* Ensures compliance with CSWE and SACSCOC.
* Promotes instructional quality across all modalities.

**Supports Student Success*** Partners with admissions, advising, practicum, recruitment, and student success.
* Advances recruitment, retention, persistence, and graduation initiatives.

**Strengthens Community Impact*** Develops relationships with agencies, alumni, professional organizations, and community partners.
* Supports fundraising and workforce partnerships.
* Expands community\-engaged scholarship and education.

**Manages Resources for Organizational Success*** Oversees personnel, budgeting, operational planning, and resource allocation.
* Collaborates with College leadership to advance strategic priorities.

The University’s mission involves three primary functions across our faculty cohort: instruction, research, and service. Each year, various ranking faculty work with the Office of the Dean to delineate their distribution of effort (DOE). This DOE outlines how faculty will spend their time. In general, DOE for faculty members in the Regular Title Series typically includes allocations in the areas of instruction, research, and service. The DOE for the Chair and Executive Director is subject to negotiation but we anticipate roughly 70% Administration, 25% research and 5% service.
  

  

Of course, the DOE can fluctuate depending on an array of factors (e.g., grant funding, new course development, service to the college, etc.). It is expected that work in this faculty appointment, including but not limited to course instruction, office hours, administrative meetings, and attending college\-wide events such as faculty meetings, will occur on\-site.  

  

Employment at UK is subject to fund availability and comes with many rewards, focusing on your total well\-being and career development, with leadership striving to provide a strong work\-life integration. The university generously contributes to employees’ retirement plans, medical coverage, and life insurance. In addition, UK offers optional benefits such as dental and vision insurance, additional retirement plans and much more. To learn more about these benefits, please visit: **https://hr.uky.edu/employment/our\-benefits**.

**Director Of Operations**

*Our mantra is simple \- love. Love what you do. Love where you live. Love the success and return we provide. At RR Living, we are a part of something special.*


The Director of Operations is a key leadership position responsible for growing a team of people who will effectively execute the company’s business strategy. Operational leaders are empowered to drive the financial success of multi\-million\-dollar communities and assets within a defined portfolio/region while providing strategic leadership, management oversight and accountability for several areas of performance including property operations, portfolio financial results, compliance, talent acquisition, team member development, customer and resident satisfaction, asset preservation, service, facilities \& expense control. You ensure that established business strategy and financial performance targets are achieved or exceeded.


**Responsibilities**

* You and your community teams are expected to drive operational improvement including increasing physical and economic occupancy at the communities assigned to you. This will be accomplished through hiring and developing a stable well\-trained team of professionals who understand the RR Living Core Values and drive excellence at the community and with resident satisfaction.

Operational leaders are empowered to drive the financial success of multi\-million\-dollar communities and assets within a defined portfolio/region while providing strategic leadership, management oversight and accountability for several areas of performance including property operations, portfolio financial results, compliance, talent acquisition, team member development, customer and resident satisfaction, asset preservation, service, facilities \& expense control. You ensure that established business strategy and financial performance targets are achieved or exceeded.


**Responsibilities**

* You and your community teams are expected to drive operational improvement including increasing physical and economic occupancy at the communities assigned to you. This will be accomplished through hiring and developing a stable well\-trained team of professionals who understand the RR Living Core Values and drive excellence at the community and with resident satisfaction.
* You are expected to achieve Budgeted Income, Expenses and CNOI every month, quarter, and year on the assets you are responsible for.
* Proactively recognize trends and market conditions that may impact property performance. Become an expert on the markets you are in, know your competition and how those communities align with our community.
* Using strategy and experience, successfully lead through economic downturns to ensure the assets under your direction are leading the market in performance and proforma budget achievement.
* Achieve and maintain delinquency at less than 2% on stabilized assets. On assigned assets above 2%, goal percentages will be developed during your first 30 days of employment, to outline tiered expectations to ultimately achieve the 2% or better goal on each asset within 90 days.
* Achieve portfolio and proforma occupancy goals and maintaining a 95% or above occupancy
* Grow rental rate and income in accordance with ownership business strategies and assigned budget, and at a minimum striving to achieve 2% more than market average.
* Build a team of direct reports and community team members that understand the importance of executing an exemplary resident experience, receiving excellent and respectful service every day.
* Ensure your portfolio pays attention to the details, including curb appeal, a safe and enjoyable community atmosphere, well maintained amenities, and rental homes where residents are proud to have family and friends visit.
* Ensure communities are well\-maintained physically, including make\-readies, preventive maintenance, and the completion of service requests within 48 hours of submission.
* Ensure communities in your portfolio achieve net move\-in goals, retention and rate expectations and administrative reporting that is on time and accurate.
* Hire, train, mentor and develop future leaders and community team members. Proactively manage underperformers by training them, developing them and respectfully off boarding those who are not performing.
* Frequently conduct physical property walks, including the inspection of all grounds, community spaces such as hallways, breezeways, vacant apartment homes, clubhouses, shops, amenity areas, entrance and exit areas and community offices to ensure cleanliness, condition and that all areas are in good working order.
* Quickly learn how to navigate and use the computer software programs utilized by the company including Real Page One Site, On\-Site, AppFolio, Knock, Buzz, Apartment IQ Rentable, and more.
* Maintain ethical, professional, respectful, and courteous relationships with residents, teammates, and other customers. Follow all local, federal, and state regulations including Fair Housing Guidelines
* Act as an Ambassador of RR Living building relationships in the surrounding neighborhoods and community, and in our RR Giving Impact Initiatives.
* Ask questions, think strategically and lead your team with a Founder’s Mentality while being an integral and key part of the property management leadership team.

**RR Living's Core Values**

* **Be Your Best. Do Your Best.**

*We celebrate individualism, collaboration, and inclusion. Our associates are the best in the business, exemplifying that which we celebrate as an organization. Recognizing happiness and great attitudes are contagious, we hold ourselves and each other accountable. Success begets success and happiness begets happiness***.**




* **Honesty, Integrity, and an Unwavering Commitment to Excellence:**

*Excellent resident experiences are our specialty, recognizing the unique challenges of rentership. We provide a wonderful place to call Home, striving to do what is often missed \- creating unparalleled living experiences for our residents, incredible opportunities for our associates, and impressive revenues for our partners \&; owners.* ***Simply put, we Care.***




* **Empowered Associates, Obsessively Purpose\-Driven and Stronger Together:**

*Success, a people\-centric approach, and revenue growth are not independent of each other. We operate as one team. deliberate in the actions taken to drive revenue and improved valuation for owners \& investors. As happy performers, our associates are an engaged team empowered to work together to achieve our common goals, making us an unstoppable successful organization***.**




* **The Magic is in the Details:**

*Recognizing that residents choose to live where they can be proud of residing, we understand that details matter. Our teams provide personalized service that exceeds expectations and creates unique neighborhood\-like environments. From elite resident events to local partnerships

jobs.title: Senior Director of Development
jobs.description:
**POSITION TITLE:** Senior Director of Development

 **CLASSIFICATION:** Exempt

 **STATUS:** Full\-Time

 **DEPARTMENT:** Advancement

 **REPORTS TO:** Vice President of Advancement

 **SUPERVISES:** N/A

 **POSITION SUMMARY*****:***


Kentucky Wesleyan College seeks a collaborative, strategic, and relationship\-driven fundraising professional to serve as Senior Director of Development. This leadership position is responsible for expanding philanthropic support through the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of major and planned gift donors.


The Senior Director manages a portfolio of approximately 100–150 major gift prospects and donors, developing personalized engagement strategies that inspire transformational philanthropy. Working in partnership with Advancement colleagues, academic leadership, faculty, alumni, volunteers, and community stakeholders, this position advances the College's mission by securing significant philanthropic investments that support institutional priorities and student success.


The successful candidate is an experienced frontline fundraiser who combines strong relationship\-building skills with strategic planning, data\-informed decision\-making, and a commitment to exceptional donor experiences. This position contributes to a culture of philanthropy through collaboration, innovation, accountability, and measurable fundraising outcomes.

 **PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Develop and execute strategies to identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward major and planned gift prospects in support of Kentucky Wesleyan College's mission and strategic priorities.
* Manage a portfolio of approximately 100\-150 major gift prospects and donors, with a focus on donor retention, upgrades, long\-term engagement, and gifts of significant philanthropic impact.
* Conduct regular discovery, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship visits with alumni, friends, parents, and community partners, utilizing data\-informed moves management practices.
* Develop individualized donor engagement and solicitation strategies that align donor interests with institutional funding priorities and increase philanthropic support.
* Build and maintain a healthy major gift pipeline through prospect research, qualification, tracking, forecasting, and collaboration with Advancement colleagues.
* Partner with faculty, staff, and campus leaders to create meaningful donor engagement opportunities and strengthen relationships across the College community.
* Lead and support donor stewardship and recognition efforts, ensuring donors are meaningfully engaged, acknowledged, and informed about the impact of their philanthropy.
* Collaborate with Advancement colleagues to develop compelling donor communications, promote institutional impact, and share alumni, student, and donor success stories.
* Assist in the planning and execution of donor cultivation, stewardship, recognition, and advancement events.
* Maintain accurate donor records, contact reports, and prospect activity within the College's constituent relationship management system.
* Serve as a strategic partner to Advancement leadership by contributing to fundraising strategy, revenue growth initiatives, and best practices in donor engagement.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the Vice President for Advancement.

 **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**


Bachelor’s degree; minimum of two years of experience in major gift fundraising preferably in an educational environment; a proven and verifiable track record of success in identifying, cultivating, and soliciting major gifts.

 **REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:**

* Clear understanding of moves management in professional fundraising.
* Proven ability to successfully identify and build relationships with donors to connect their interests with opportunities in a higher education or other nonprofit organization.
* Basic understanding of planned gift concepts.
* A demonstrated ability to engage and effectively communicate with diverse audiences.
* Excellent oral, written, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to persuasively articulate institutional impact and funding needs.
* Strong work ethic, self\-awareness, and ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with colleagues across campus.
* Ability and willingness to travel, work occasional evenings and weekends, and participate in donor and institutional events as needed.
* Valid driver's license or ability to obtain reliable transportation for travel related to fundraising and constituent engagement activities.

 **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Ability to develop and execute fundraising plans with strong support of metrics.
* High level of creativity, initiative, and motivation.
* Demonstrated knowledge of all facets of fundraising, including annual fund, corporate and foundation relations, planned giving, stewardship, major gift fundraising, etc.
* Ability to work cross\-functionally with academic and administrative leaders in a collaborative environment to conceive and implement innovative ideas.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and experience working in a CRM or other relational database such as Blackbaud Raiser’s Edge.
* Knowledge of best practices in alumni engagement, board and volunteer cultivation and development, project implementation and evaluation.

**WORK HOURS/CONDITIONS:**


Office environment; 40 hours per week; normally 8:00 a.m.\-5:00 p.m.; some evening and weekend work required.

jobs.title: Director of Marketing and Communications
jobs.description:
JGA’s clients are achieving important successes across the nation in Education, Healthcare, the Arts, and Human Services, and we empower and accelerate generosity in support of their work.

Johnson, Grossnickle and Associates (JGA) is a philanthropic consulting firm that is **employee\-owned.** Our members are a collaborative team of experienced professionals with deep expertise committed to innovation in the nonprofit sector. We partner with clients on fundraising strategies to advance their philanthropic goals.

We are growing and are currently seeking a **Director of Marketing and Communications** to join our team.

The Director of Marketing and Communications leads JGA’s efforts to effectively drive a strategic marketing approach ensuring close alignment with the sales enablement strategy. Thie Director leads and implements marketing and communication for JGA and reports to a Senior Consultant.

The successful candidate will work effectively within a team\-oriented and mission\-driven environment. Strategy, strong communication, and self\-motivation are crucial to success. JGA takes a thoughtful approach to philanthropic consulting and acts as a guide in philanthropy; we are authentic counselors to our diverse clientele, and this position will help reflect this externally.

This is a full\-time, hybrid position, with expected travel to the office at least 3 days a week to attend in\-person meetings in our office just south of Indianapolis in Greenwood, Indiana.

**Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Lead JGA’s marketing efforts that support the goals of the JGA strategic plan, build our national presence in the nonprofit sector, and accelerate our growing strategic partnerships.
* Implement strategy on marketing, communications, and brand presence ensuring it aligns with the firm’s overall sales enablement efforts. This includes conferences, JGA hosted in\-person events, webinars, blogs, and social media.
* Coordinate content development, daily marketing outreach, and website and social media presence, in close partnership with the Director of Business Development.
* Strategize with JGA consultants regarding thought leadership blogs, speaking opportunities, publications, and cross\-industry collaborations.
* Monitor the effectiveness of core marketing channels and shift resources to maximize return on investment.

**Preferred qualifications include:**

* Strategic leader who can learn quickly, communicate well, and proactively generate ideas and solutions.
* Passion for philanthropy, for accelerating the missions of nonprofits and the good they do in the world.
* An action\-focused team player who is energized by meeting goals creatively and collaboratively.
* Excellent organizational skills (oral and written) and the ability to excel at details, multitasking, and working under pressure.
* Engaged and positive teamworking capability with everyone at JGA.
* Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, or related field.
* Familiarity with constituent CRMs, web content management, and email communication platforms. (HubSpot, WordPress, Microsoft, and Adobe products).
* Five or more years of marketing experience with a variety of marketing channels (web, digital, social media, email, and print.)
* Experience across various marketing functions including brand identity, demand generation, sales pipeline, thought leadership, and events.

**Physical requirements:**

* Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer and talking on the phone.
* Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.

**JGA’s Commitment to Diversity:**

**We are committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion.** We work to advance equity, access, and inclusion of diverse people and perspectives in our work as a team, with our clients, in the philanthropic sector, and in the community.

Guided by our JGA values, we are authentically engaged in this work and monitoring, reflecting on, and adjusting our approaches when needed. We are focused on:

* continuing to diversify our team;
* strengthening our DEI competencies in our work with clients; and
* Ensuring our partnerships and work in the community, meaningfully reflect and advance our DEI priorities.

**Compensation, Benefits, and Perks**

* Competitive salary based on experience
* Medical/dental/vision options for employee and dependents
* Voluntary benefit options
* Employee Assistance Plan (EAP)
* Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP)
* 401(k)
* Generous PTO plan that increases with tenure
* 12 paid holidays
* Holiday break during the week between December 25th and December 31st
* Paid parental leave
* Volunteer time off
* Hybrid working options
* Individualized onboarding plan
* Individual development plans (IDP)
* Professional development opportunities
* $50/month cellphone reimbursement

*This job description is an overview of the primary responsibilities and qualifications for this position. We value agility, flexibility, and growth potential, so this job description is not inclusive of all duties you might be asked to perform or of all qualifications that may be required either now or in the future.*

Pay: $80,000\.00 \- $95,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
