* Employee assistance program
* Flexible schedule
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Paid time off
* Parental leave
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Education:

* Bachelor's (Preferred)

Experience:

* Marketing: 5 years (Preferred)

Ability to Commute:

* Greenwood, IN 46143 (Required)

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Greenwood, IN 46143

jobs.description:
**POSITION:** Arts Program Director (Full\-time/Non\-Exempt)

**RESUME AND COVER LETTER WILL BE RECEIVED UNTIL THIS POSITION IS FILLED**

**ORGANIZATION DESCRIPTION:** IBA**\-**Inquilinos Boricuas en Accion empowers and engages individuals and families to improve their lives through high\-quality affordable housing, education, and arts programs.

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Program Development and Management**

* Business driven individual.
* Develops and implements the Arts program business plan.
* Develops and oversees year\-long programming for the IBA Arts Program, including flagship summer events: Festival Betances and Tito Puente Latin Music Series.
* Develops arts placemaking activities and initiatives in La CASA and Villa Victoria.

**Partnerships and Collaboration**

* Fosters arts and cultural relationships to cultivate external partnerships and collaborations.
* Maintains partnerships with local colleges, organizations, and artists to help produce high\-caliber arts programming.
* Works collaboratively with IBA Program Directors and the Chief Program Officer (CPO) to integrate arts into IBA's programs.
* Collaborates with IBA's staff to promote programmatic objectives within our organizational mission.
* Collaborates with the communications department to promote the program and events.

**Reporting and Data Management**

* Maintains data collection, tracking, and reporting regarding artists, clients, audience participation, referrals, and program outputs/outcomes.
* Prepares necessary management reports for IBA's Board of Directors, funding sources, Finance, and others as needed.

**Financial Oversight and Revenue Generation**

* Ensures contracting and outsourcing compliance with financial, legal, safety, and regulatory requirements related to artist contracts, licenses, etc.
* Develops, implements, and oversees strategies to increase revenue through ticket sales and sponsorship.
* Works closely with IBA's CEO, COO, CFO, and Chief Program Officer to build a realistic and sustainable budget and develop specific performance measures.
* Works with the Chief Program Officer and Chief Philanthropy Officer to increase fundraising, grant writing, and reporting.

**Team Leadership and Representation**

* Oversees the arts team.
* Represents the organization at external meetings as needed.
* Participates fully in the organization's annual events such as Three Kings Day, Membership Drive, Board Election, Festival Betances, and other community\-related events.
* Carries out ad hoc duties as needed.

**SKILLS / QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Arts Administration, or a related field preferred.
* Three to five years of proven successful experience in: planning, managing and implementing arts programs activities, staff management, fundraising, budget development/financial management and strategic planning.
* Excellent verbal and written communications skills.
* Bilingual, Spanish\-English, preferred.
* Strong administrative, organizational skills and attentive to details.
* Ability to manage multiple tasks accurately and within deadlines.
* Ability to work autonomously and in a team setting.
* Experience with program evaluation, data collection and analysis.
* High degree of computer literacy with excellent knowledge of word processing, spreadsheet and database software application required.

**COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS**


IBA is proud to offer very competitive $105,000 annualized salary, commensurate with experience, and a robust benefit plan that includes an 80/20 premium cost share for comprehensive health, dental and vision insurance; a generous HRA provided by the company ($10,000 or $20,000 based on single and family coverage) and other built in supports that significantly reduces or eliminates out of pocket medical expenses. We offer a 403b plan with annual employer contribution, generous paid time off and free parking (limited availability).

**Work Culture:**


IBA is located in Boston's historic South End in the multiculturally rich community of Villa Victoria. We value teamwork and collaboration, believe in developing leaders and foster a culture of excellence. Our commitment to inclusion, equity, empowerment and community building is inherent in IBA's mission, imbedded in our values and demonstrated in the ways we work together to achieve mission impact and outcome goal.

jobs.title: Director of Philanthropy and Strategic Partnerships
jobs.description:
Description:  



**Director of Philanthropy and Strategic Partnerships**

**Grade:** 16  

**Salary Range:** $92,300 \- $110,700

**Location:** Indianapolis, Indiana (Hybrid)

**Reports to:** Executive Director

**Supervises:** Development Staff

**Travel:** Significant Statewide

**Organizational Overview**


The ACLU of Indiana is a nonpartisan organization dedicated to protecting and expanding civil liberties and civil rights across the state. Through integrated advocacy, policy, legal, communications, and operational strategies, we work to defend constitutional rights, dismantle systemic barriers, and advance lasting structural change. As our advocacy and public engagement efforts continue to expand, philanthropy plays a critical role in mobilizing the resources, partnerships, and statewide support necessary to advance our mission.

**Position Summary**


The Director of Philanthropy and Strategic Partnerships serves as the organization's senior fundraising strategist and relationship builder, leading efforts to secure the philanthropic investments necessary to advance the ACLU of Indiana's advocacy, litigation, public education, and organizational priorities.


Working as a strategic partner to the Executive Director, this leader develops and executes a comprehensive fundraising strategy while cultivating meaningful relationships with major donors, foundations, business leaders, and influential stakeholders throughout Indiana. The Director of Philanthropy helps translate emerging civil liberties issues and organizational priorities into compelling philanthropic investment opportunities that strengthen the organization's statewide impact.


This position requires an experienced development executive who possesses deep knowledge of Indiana's philanthropic, civic, political, and community landscape and can build authentic relationships across diverse constituencies throughout both urban and rural communities.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Develop and implement a comprehensive fundraising strategy aligned with organizational priorities, advocacy initiatives, and long\-term growth objectives.
* Partner with the Executive Director to establish multi\-year fundraising strategies that support the organization's evolving advocacy and public engagement priorities.
* Build and maintain strategic relationships with philanthropic leaders, foundations, business executives, community organizations, and civic partners throughout Indiana to expand the organization's visibility, influence, and fundraising capacity.
* Lead all major\-gift, foundation, corporate, and planned giving strategies, cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding high\-capacity donors and institutional funders.
* Identify emerging philanthropic opportunities by monitoring statewide political, legislative, demographic, and community trends and translating those opportunities into sustainable revenue strategies.
* Collaborate closely with Legal and Public Engagement staff to develop compelling donor engagement strategies that connect supporters to the organization's impact and long\-term vision.
* Partner with the Executive Director and Board of Directors to cultivate donor relationships, strengthen philanthropic engagement, and advance a culture of philanthropy throughout the organization.
* Expand the organization's statewide philanthropic presence by cultivating new supporters, strengthening regional partnerships, and increasing engagement outside Central Indiana.
* Oversee donor communications, stewardship strategies, and acknowledgment processes that build long\-term donor loyalty and investment.
* Supervise, support, and grow Development staff while fostering a high\-performing, collaborative, and innovative fundraising culture.
* Oversee fundraising systems, prospect research, donor analytics, and reporting to ensure strategic decision\-making and effective portfolio management.
* Track fundraising performance, evaluate key performance indicators, analyze trends, and develop strategic revenue projections in partnership with the Senior Director of Finance to inform budgeting, long\-range financial planning, and recommendations to executive leadership and the Board of Directors.
* Perform other duties as assigned.


Requirements:
* Ten or more years of progressively responsible leadership experience in nonprofit fundraising, philanthropy, institutional advancement, or related executive leadership roles.
* Demonstrated success in securing major gifts, foundation grants, and institutional partnerships resulting in significant organizational growth.
* Extensive knowledge of Indiana's philanthropic, civic, political, and nonprofit landscape, with demonstrated experience cultivating relationships throughout both urban and rural communities.
* Demonstrated ability to engage senior executives, elected officials, community leaders, board members, foundations, and high\-capacity donors around complex public policy or mission\-driven initiatives.
* Experience developing long\-term fundraising strategies that align philanthropic investment with organizational priorities and measurable impact.
* Proven ability to build strategic partnerships across diverse sectors, including business, philanthropy, government, healthcare, higher education, and community organizations.
* Strong strategic planning, organizational leadership, and project management skills.
* Excellent written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
* Demonstrated ability to analyze complex information, exercise sound judgment, and manage multiple priorities in a fast\-paced environment.
* Commitment to the mission, values, and nonpartisan work of the ACLU.
* Demonstrated commitment to working collaboratively with individuals from diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives.
* Candidates must have a valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and be available to travel as needed.


The ACLU of Indiana is an equal opportunity and affirmative act

jobs.description:
**Position Summary****:**


The University of Arizona Foundation is seeking a motivated and goal\-oriented professional to join the Philanthropy \& Alumni Engagement team as a Director of Development (DOD) for the College of Medicine – Tucson. The successful candidate will work to secure gifts of $50,000 or more to further the goals and objectives of the College.


The DOD will be a key member of this development team reporting to the Senior Director of Development for the College. This position is a member of the Philanthropy and Alumni Engagement Team (PAE) and subject to joint management by the University of Arizona and the University of Arizona Foundation as specified in the restated Development Services and Asset Management Agreement dated July 2, 2021\.


The University of Arizona College of Medicine – Tucson (COM\-T) is transforming academic medicine through innovative undergraduate medical education and postgraduate training programs; strategic, interdisciplinary trans\-institutional research; collaborative health care delivery; and a strong, diverse, and engaged faculty.


COM\-T provides state\-of\-the\-art programs of medical education, groundbreaking research opportunities, and leading\-edge patient care. Founded on the campus of the University of Arizona (University) in 1967 as the state’s only MD degree\-granting college and a resource for the people of Arizona, today the College of Medicine ranks among the top medical schools in the nation for research and primary care. From an initial class of just 32 students, the College of Medicine today has graduated more than 5,000 physicians. College of Medicine students, faculty, staff, and alumni today continue more than 50 years of service in advancing medical care and knowledge in Arizona—and around the world.


The College’s integrated, multidisciplinary curriculum combines the latest advances in biomedical science with the practice of the classical art of medicine. In 2015, The University partnered with Banner Health, the fourth\-largest healthcare corporation in the country, which serves as COM\-T’s primary clinical partner. In addition, affiliations with more than a dozen hospitals and healthcare facilities across two campuses ensure that students will always have access to groundbreaking research opportunities, world\-class faculty, and meaningful patient\-care experiences. A strong engagement and fundraising program is a critical component of COM\-T’s strategic plan. Increased private philanthropy from alumni, grateful patients, community members, institutional funders, friends, and other constituencies is vital to the COM\-T’s future impact on the health of people in Arizona, the nation, and the world. COM\-T is part of the University of Arizona Health Sciences (UAHS), a statewide leader in biomedical research and health professions training. UAHS is comprised of the University of Arizona Colleges of Medicine (Phoenix and Tucson), Nursing, Pharmacy, and Mel and Enid Zuckerman College of Public Health; the University of Arizona Cancer Center; and 23 centers and institutes dedicated to research and patient care, with main campus locations in Tucson and the growing Biomedical Campus in downtown Phoenix.

**Supervisory Responsibility:**


None

**Duties \& Responsibilities****:**

* At the direction of the Senior Director of Development, lead key fundraising priority initiatives for the College. Serve as a leadership partner with key department heads, center directors, and administrators on fundraising priorities and development operations initiatives.
* Develop and sustain strong relationships with the College/unit leadership, faculty, board members, alumni, volunteers, donors, and financial professionals.
* Responsible for building and maintaining a healthy portfolio defined for DODs as 50\-70 assigned prospects with 40\-50 in cultivation/solicitation; 40% of those in cultivation/solicitation capacity rated at $250L\+ and 10% rated at $1M\+.
* Effectively initiate and complete Qualification Plans per PAE standards to develop new major gift prospects.
* After an initial 6\-month onboarding period, execute an agreed\-upon metric of at least 100 current or prospect donor meetings and the successful closure of 15\+ major/principal gift proposals per year, with an expectation of $1M\+ raised after the initial onboarding period (with incremental increases after the first year).
* Serve as a member of the College of Medicine – Tucson development team, working collaboratively with the alumni and stewardship positions, as well as various academic faculty and staff.
* Develop and execute strategic, personalized cultivation, solicitation and stewardship plans for an assigned portfolio ($50,000 capacity or greater) of donor prospects (individual, corporate, and foundation) through personal meetings (in\-person or via live video conferencing platforms), letters, phone calls, email, text messaging, and other methods.
* Plan, coordinate, and schedule weekly personal meetings with prospects and donors utilizing UAF software, introductory letters, emails/texts, and phone calls to set appointments.
* Provide a high level of support in stewardship and recognition efforts for annual fund donors.
* Develop personalized strategies for all assigned donors and prospects which builds, maintains, and enhances relationships while furthering donors’ philanthropic objectives.
* Collaborate with the Dean and Senior Director of Development on the strategic planning of new projects and initiatives with specific fundraising goals for the College of Medicine – Tucson.
* Design and manage solicitation and stewardship plans in UAF CRM platform to support fundraising initiatives.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Money Follows the Person/Transition \& Diversion Program (MFP/TDP) Program Director provides leadership, oversight, and administration for DCIL's MFP and TDP programs. This position ensures that program services, work plans, referrals, documentation, expenditures, and required reports comply with applicable state and federal requirements, contractual expectations, and DCIL policies while reflecting the organization's mission and the Independent Living Philosophy.

The Program Director supervises MFP/TDP staff; coordinates the assignment and monitoring of referrals; supports consumer transitions from institutional settings to community living; and ensures that services are person\-centered, timely, accurately documented, and responsive to each individual's goals, choices, risks, and support needs. The position reviews consumer and program records in Therap and CIL Suite, conducts routine quality\-assurance audits, monitors follow\-up activities, and addresses documentation or service delivery concerns.

This position works collaboratively with consumers, families, guardians, transition coordinators, MFP/TDP administrators, HCBS representatives, community providers, Housing, DCIL leadership, and other partners. The Program Director facilitates meetings, supports staff training and development, promotes coordinated service delivery, and represents DCIL professionally in program, community, and interagency activities.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES \& RESPONSIBILITIES**

1\. Develop and maintain an understanding of DCIL's mission, programs, services, policies, history, and the IL Philosophy, as well as MFP/TDP requirements, guidance, work plans, and contractual expectations.

2\. Provide day\-to\-day leadership, direction, and supervision to MFP/TDP staff, including assigning duties, monitoring workloads, supporting case consultation, addressing performance concerns, and promoting consistent service delivery.

3\. Coordinate the receipt, review, assignment, tracking, and follow\-up of MFP and TDP referrals to ensure timely contact, appropriate action, and continuity of services.

4\. Ensure consumers receive person centered support, advocacy, skills training, referrals, and transition related assistance that promote informed choice, community living, independence, and self\-determination.

5\. Review referral, transition, termination, Information and Referral (I\&R), re\-institutionalization, and ongoing case documentation in Therap and CIL Suite for accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and compliance.

6\. Conduct and document quality\-assurance audits at least monthly of required MFP/TDP records, including Transition Assessments, Transition Plans, Risk Assessments, backup plans, case notes, supporting documentation, and applicable database records.

7\. Monitor consumer progress, service barriers, health and safety concerns, transition risks, and unmet needs; work with staff and program partners to resolve concerns and support successful community transitions.

8\. Complete and submit accurate monthly, quarterly, annual, grant, and other required program reports within established deadlines, including reports requested by MFP/TDP administrators and DCIL leadership.

9\. Monitor program statistics, outcomes, expenditures, service authorizations, and supporting documentation to ensure compliance with funding requirements and approved program activities.

10\. Develop, review, update, and implement the annual MFP/TDP work plan, program procedures, goals, timelines, and quality\-improvement activities in collaboration with the Executive Director and appropriate DCIL staff.

11\. Facilitate and participate in MFP/HCBS territory meetings, program staffing, transition meetings, and other meetings with MFP/TDP administrators, staff, consumers, and community partners.

12\. Develop and maintain effective working relationships with state agencies, HCBS representatives, transition coordinators, service providers, housing resources, community organizations, and other partners involved in supporting community living.

13\. Provide clear and timely communication to consumers, families, guardians, staff, and partners regarding referrals, program processes, services, documentation requirements, and follow\-up responsibilities.

14\. Assist with recruiting, interviewing, hiring, onboarding, and training MFP/TDP staff; coordinate initial and ongoing training to ensure staff understand program requirements, consumer documentation, data entry, confidentiality, and DCIL services.

15\. Conduct regular supervision meetings, probationary reviews, and annual performance evaluations in coordination with the Executive Director, and provide timely coaching, feedback, and corrective direction when needed.

16\. Collaborate with the Executive Director, IL Program Director, Board of Directors, and other DCIL staff on strategic planning, policy development, outreach, education, and organizational goals.

17\. Work cooperatively with staff in both DCIL offices to promote consistency in service delivery, referrals, documentation, policies, procedures, outreach, education, and community engagement.

18\. Represent DCIL and promote MFP/TDP services through professional communication, outreach, presentations, community events, interagency collaboration, and systems advocacy activities.

19\. Maintain strict confidentiality, safeguard consumer and agency information, and comply with all applicable laws, program requirements, and DCIL policies and procedures.

20\. Travel as needed to meet consumer and program needs, attend meetings and trainings, monitor services, and carry out assigned responsibilities throughout DCIL's service area.

21\. Perform other reasonable duties as assigned by the Executive Director.

jobs.description:
**The Opportunity**


The University of Central Florida (UCF) Health Student Health Services is seeking applications for a full\-time, non\-tenure\-earning assistant, associate or professor of medicine and Executive Director of Student Health Services.

**Primary Duties**: The Executive Director will be responsible for the formulation, development, and supervision of Student Health Services. This includes, but not limited to, the areas of administration, personnel, budget planning, and internal communication.

* Leads the development, implementation, and oversight of the Student Health Services Strategic Plan while managing a multi\-million\-dollar budget, including financial planning, expenditure approval, resource allocation, and future program and facility expansion, renovation, and maintenance initiatives.
* Chairs the Student Health Services (SHS) Executive Council and the SHS Performance Improvement Committee, providing leadership for program evaluation, quality improvement initiatives, strategic planning, and resource management.
* Ensures that the university's goals and objectives are communicated and achieved.
* Represents UCF Student Health Services at the university, state, regional, and national levels with active participation and leadership in constituent organizations.
* Leads Student Health Services in all Emergency Response situations (Hurricanes, Fires, Active Shooter and others).
* Represents Student Health Services and provides medical input and expertise to other university units and departments.
* Establishes operational policies for Student Health Services and interprets University of Central Florida Board of Trustees policies as they relate to student health.
* Works closely with the College of Medicine Associate Dean for Clinical Affairs to coordinate Student Health Services in response to any UCF infectious disease outbreak or threat of outbreak.
* Provides leadership and oversight for workforce planning and staffing operations across Student Health Services, ensuring appropriate staffing levels, operational efficiency, and staff productivity. Promotes and advances Student Health Services through engagement and collaboration with key university partners, including Student Government Association (SGA), Housing and Residence Life, Greek Life, and Graduate Studies.
* Provides leadership and policy direction, ensuring a formal business plan is developed, periodically updated, and followed.
* Ensures regulatory compliance withstrict adherence to federal and state laws, including HIPAA, FERPA, and public health reporting mandates.
* Develops and directs studies for program analysis and evaluation to ensure proper management of available resources.
* Ensures professional standards meet requirements of licensing agencies and guidelines established by the Accreditation Association for Ambulatory Health Care (AAAHC), including maintaining accreditation.
* Ensures clinical activities comply with Student Health Services policies, state and federal statutes, and Board of Regents guidelines.
* Advises and assists in planning, directing, and reporting clinical service activities.
* Provides direct clinical services to patients and consultative support to medical staff as needed.
* May supervise medical students, interns, and residents during their rotations.
* Fosters the development of comprehensive clinical care, education, and prevention programs, and assumes responsibility for the development of medical services and programs.
* Engages in frequent internal and external collaborations through committees, task forces, partnerships, and public relations efforts; participates in campus\-wide health promotion.
* Oversight of the Student Health Insurance Plan (SHIP).
* Completes all required university, division, and departmental training in a timely manner.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* M.D. or D.O. degree from an accredited institution with a license to practice in the State of Florida.
* The candidate’s scholarly background and experience must be commensurate with the faculty rank for which the application is submitted.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Demonstrated experience in college health leadership, administration, or student health services.
* Has a strong understanding of higher education dynamics, with success in fostering cross\-functional partnerships with campus and academic stakeholders to advance student health initiatives, programs, and services.
* Board certified in Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, Emergency Medicine, Pediatrics, Sports Medicine, Psychiatry, or other relevant specialties. Experience providing direct patient care in outpatient, inpatient, emergency, or other clinical settings.
* Prior clinical and administrative experience within a higher education student health center is strongly preferred, with experience leading or supporting public health initiatives and population health programs.
* Minimum of five years of professional related experience.

**Additional Application Materials Required:**


UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

* A curriculum vitae.
* A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as research agenda and teaching experience/interest.

**NOTE**: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.


The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.


Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Nicole.Calderon\-Morales@ucf.edu; a

**Job Summary**

The **Executive Director of the Little Compton Community Center (LCCC)** serves as the chief administrative officer for the organization. This leader manages the daily operations, multi\-generational programming, and financial sustainability of a private501(c)(3\) non\-profit, which acts as a central hub for Little Compton’s 3,500 residents. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director oversees a team of dedicated staff and volunteers, shapes community engagement, and maintains a safe, welcoming multi\-use facility.

Under the oversight of the Board of Directors, the Executive Director leads fundraising, operations, and community\-driven program design to serve all age demographics—from toddlers to senior citizens. * **Experience:** 5\+ years of progressive leadership experience in a community hub or non\-profit setting.

* **Technical Proficiency:** Hands\-on experience managing organization financials in QuickBooks and coordinating across virtual meeting platforms (e.g., Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google suite and Blackbaud/E\-Tapestry).
* **Digital Communication Skills:** Proven capability to execute website maintenance, design email campaigns, utilize digital scheduling software, and navigate major social media platforms.
* **Regulatory Compliance:** Proven familiarity with State of Rhode Island health, sanitation, and child care licensing processes.
* **Communication Skills:** Proficient in both written and oral communication. Comfortable speaking publicly in small and large group settings. Experience managing conflict with both staff and outside parties. Possesses cross\-generational relationship\-building skills.

Join us as we build a thriving community center that empowers residents through innovative programs and meaningful connections!

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule
* Paid time off

**EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR JOB DESCRIPTION**

**Location:** Los Angeles, CA

**Job Type:** Full\-Time, hybrid

**About LocoL**

Alta Community (dba LocoL) is a nonprofit in Watts, which provides culinary job training and education for young people while addressing food insecurity through the preparation and distribution of affordable, high\-quality meals, primarily for local nonprofits. Founded as a nonprofit in 2023 by chefs Keith Corbin and Daniel Patterson, LocoL is on the site of the former LocoL restaurant, originally founded by chefs Roy Choi and Daniel Patterson.

**Position Summary**

The Executive Director reports to the Board of Directors and has overall authority and accountability for organizational strategy, personnel, operations, programs, fundraising, and financial management, within policies and budgets approved by the Board.

The Executive Director will lead Alta Community/LocoL through its next stage of organizational development, strengthening the systems, partnerships, revenue, team, and strategy required to deliver sustainable community impact. The Executive Director will have overall responsibility for organizational leadership, fundraising and earned\-revenue growth, financial stewardship, program quality and impact, team development, and external relationships.

This is an opportunity for a hands\-on, entrepreneurial leader who can move comfortably between long\-term strategy and practical execution. The successful candidate will understand how to build an emerging nonprofit organization while respecting LocoL’s history, community relationships, culinary identity, and commitment to economic opportunity and food justice.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Leadership, Strategy \& Administration**

* In partnership with the board of directors, develop and execute a strategic plan for the next five years of growth and impact.
* Ensure operational and programmatic alignment with the organization’s values and goals.
* Engage the Board through quarterly meetings to facilitate effective org governance.
* Improve and implement HR practices for employee success, including performance management, compensation and staffing, and employee development and retention.
* Build and develop a high\-performing, inclusive team, ensuring role clarity and fostering a culture of growth, accountability, and teamwork.
* Ensure compliance with California employment requirements.

**Fundraising, Communications \& Financial Management**

* Develop and implement a revenue strategy including earned income meal contracts, grants, and individual giving to raise and sustainably expand \~$700K operating budget.
* Build and maintain relationships with donors, foundations, and funding partners.
* Strengthen partnerships with nonprofits, community leaders and hiring partners.
* Leverage data to enhance organizational storytelling and external communications to grow awareness, convey impact to key stakeholders, and drive fundraising targets.
* Oversee financial planning, budgeting, and resource allocation for fiscal sustainability, including cash\-flow management, financial controls, monthly financial reporting and forecasting, grant reporting, insurance and risk management and earned income margins.
* Ensure compliance with all appropriate tax and accounting standards, as well as nonprofit regulations, reporting, and best practices.
* Oversee planning of fundraising and community events, as needed.

**Program Development**

Recruit and manage a new Program Manager to ensure organizational alignment and effective program delivery. Program Manager responsibilities include:

* Manage six program staff members and develop a hiring plan to fill additional capacity needs within the organization.
* Expand and refine programs that provide culinary training, cooking education, and affordable catering for nonprofits.
* Ensure operational success for LocoL, including kitchen operations, quality control, menu development, budgets, vendor relationships and customer service.
* Collaborate with chef leaders at LocoL to develop and implement a job training program, focusing on culinary skills, hospitality, and professional development.
* Mentor and coach team members, many of whom are entering the workforce for the first time, to help them achieve their full potential.
* Oversee outcome measurement to demonstrate effectiveness.

**Required capabilities**

* Passion for community and workforce development, food justice, and economic empowerment.
* Proven executive or senior leadership in nonprofit management, social enterprises, or related fields.
* Experience partnering with board of directors and leading teams.
* Strong track record in fundraising, grants, and financial management.
* Excellent strategic thinking, communication, storytelling, and advocacy skills.

**Strongly preferred capabilities**

* Social\-enterprise leadership.
* Food, culinary, hospitality, catering, or production experience.
* Los Angeles or Watts community relationships.
* Early\-stage organizational building.
* Brand and communications experience.
* Government contracting or institutional meal contracts.

**Compensation \& Benefits**

* Salary Range: $90,000\-$110,000 (commensurate with experience).
* Stipend for healthcare.
* Paid\-time off and paid sick time.

**How to Apply**

Interested candidates should submit a resume and cover letter to **info@altacommunityla.org** with the subject line **“Executive Director Application – LocoL.”** Priority will be given to applications received by August 31, 2026\.

Pay: $90,000\.00 \- $110,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Paid time off

People with a criminal record are encouraged to apply

The Frye Art Museum is one of Seattle's most beloved cultural institutions and one of the nation's few free art museums. Founded on the conviction that art should be accessible to everyone, the Frye has served as a welcoming gathering place for nearly 75 years—where artists, audiences, ideas, and communities come together through meaningful, unique encounters with modern and contemporary art.

  



The museum is known not only for the quality of its exhibitions and programs centered on the art of our time, but also for its culture of experimentation, curiosity, generosity, and creative joy. Highland Memorial Park Cemetery located at 1 Rhode Island Avenue, Johnston RI is a non\-denominational cemetery situated on 150 acres. The Corporation was established in 1931 and features a park\-like landscape with over 28,000 burials which are maintained in perpetuity.

The president and CEO of the Cemetery should be someone who can meet the following objectives and who contains the skill set to not only manage the day to day operations of the Cemetery, but someone who can also assist and guide families as they deal with the loss of a loved one.

1\. **Strategic \& Financial Management:**

a. Have the ability to develop and execute short\-term and long\-term strategic plans that ensure the Cemetery’s financial stability.

b. Prepare, manage, and oversee the annual budget, capital expenditures (i.e. mausoleum, chapel, land development, and heavy equipment), and plot pricing/sales.

c. Work with the financial advisors and monitor the performance of the perpetual care funds to guarantee the viability of the Cemetery property and the grounds.

d. Work with and report directly to the Board of Directors to provide periodic updates on the financial position of the Cemetery and the operations.

2\. **Operations and Maintenance:**

a. Ability to manage and lead administrative, sales, and maintenance personnel. The direct supervision of the maintenance personnel is the responsibility of the Superintendent who reports to the President/CEO.

b. Foster a professional, all inclusive, respectful, and safe working environment for all personnel. Leading by example.

c. Oversee the scheduling and coordination of burials and memorial services with Cemetery staff, grieving families, and local funeral homes.

d. Develop, monitor, and maintain operational policies, procedures, and expansion/renovation initiatives. All policies and procedures are subject to Board approval and adoption. Policies and procedures must also be in compliance with the Corporation’s bylaws.

3\. **Compliance and Risk Management:**

a. Maintain strict adherence to Federal, State, and Local statutes governing Cemetery operations and the perpetual care requirements.

b. Ensure meticulous record\-keeping regarding burial rights, plot ownership, and mapping of the Cemetery property.

4\. **Family \& Community Relations:**

a. Ensure that Cemetery personal provide compassionate, empathetic customer care to grieving families.

b. Act as the public face of the Cemetery, building beneficial relationships with the local community, funeral homes, mortuaries, governmental agencies, religious and civic organizations.

5\. **Qualifications \& Requirements:**

Bachelor’s degree with a major in business administration, finance, and/or management is preferred but not required.

Pay: $85,000\.00 \- $115,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance

Work Location: In person

new_jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
new_jobs.description:
**Three generations. Multiple plants. One operator to run them.**


Press\-Seal Corporation has been manufacturing specialty rubber sealing products for the waterworks and industrial markets for three generations, family\-owned throughout. Our products sit underground in municipal infrastructure across North America, where failure is not an option and quality is not negotiable.


We are no longer a single\-plant company. Through acquisition and organic growth, we now operate multiple manufacturing facilities across Indiana, with more expected. We are creating the role of Chief Operating Officer to run them. Ownership will still be involved in plant\-level duties.

**Purpose of Position**


Reporting directly to the CEO, the COO owns manufacturing across all Press\-Seal facilities — Fort Wayne, Jasper, InSeal, and the plants we acquire next. You will carry the operating P\&L and be measured on three things above all: throughput, cost, and margin.


You will also own all of engineering — new product development and plant\-level industrial engineering both. That means one person is accountable for what we decide to build, how fast it gets to launch, and whether the process on the floor can actually make it at cost. Few operating roles at this size carry that whole span.


This is a floor role, not a corner office. You will know the extrusion lines, presses, mixers, lathe\-cut cells, and the people running them. You will decide which work belongs at which plant, where the constraints are, and what capital is worth spending. When we buy a company, you are the one who makes the operating thesis real.

**What You’ll Own**

* Consolidated operating P\&L across all manufacturing sites
* All engineering — new product development and plant\-level industrial engineering
* Plant leadership development and accountability
* Capacity, capital planning, and constraint removal
* Quality systems (ISO 9001, IATF 16949, PPAP, NSF 61\) and EHS performance
* Materials strategy, inventory, and supply resilience
* Operating integration of acquired facilities

**What We’re Looking For**

* A decade or more of manufacturing leadership with multi\-site P\&L ownership — you have run more than one plant at the same time
* Experience leading engineering on both sides: product development timelines and plant\-level industrial engineering
* A track record integrating acquisitions or turning around underperforming operations
* Materials\-processing background: rubber, polymer, plastics, or similar — mixing, molding, or extrusion
* Real fluency in lean methods and formal quality systems
* A results record you can put numbers to


Rubber compounding or molding depth, and experience in waterworks, filtration, or tier automotive supply, will move you to the top of the list.

**Why Press\-Seal**


We are family\-owned and intend to stay that way. That means decisions get made in days, not quarters, and the person setting strategy is in the building. It also means we take a long view — we are building an operating platform, not dressing up a company for sale.


You will report to the CEO with a direct line, a real mandate, and the authority to match it.

**Summary**
-----------


Park Square Homes is on a trajectory toward becoming a top 35 national homebuilder by 2035\. The COO will serve as the operational anchor of the company — owning execution across construction, land, sales, marketing, purchasing, and customer experience while functioning as a true strategic thought partner to the CEO.


This is not a caretaker role. The incoming COO will step into a business that runs on data, moves fast, and is actively integrating AI across its operations. The CEO has high expectations, values candor, and wants a leader who will respectfully push back, engage openly on strategy, and commit fully once a direction is set. If you need to be told what to do next, this is not the right seat.

**What you'll do**
------------------

**Operational leadership \& execution**

* Own day\-to\-day operational execution across construction, land, sales, purchasing, and customer experience — living in the numbers and driving accountability through structured reporting and defined KPIs.
* Translate company growth goals into operational plans with clear owners, timelines, and measurable outcomes.
* Build and enforce a culture of process discipline, daily rhythm, and high accountability without creating bureaucracy.
* Maintain strong field presence — this role demands visibility across operations, not corner office management.

**Strategic partnership**

* Serve as the CEO's strategic co\-pilot — engaging openly, pushing back respectfully when warranted, and committing fully once a direction is set.
* Lead and develop a broad team of senior direct reports across field and office functions with high expectations and genuine investment.
* Contribute meaningfully to the company's long\-term growth strategy, including geographic expansion planning and scalability initiatives targeting top 35 national builder status by 2035\.

**Land, development \& financial oversight**

* Drive land strategy and pipeline development in close coordination with the acquisitions and development teams — deep, hands\-on land experience is a non\-negotiable for this role.
* Manage banking and financing relationships in support of land and construction draws, lot banking structures, and development financing.
* Support capital deployment decisions and operational scalability investments tied to the company's aggressive growth objectives.

**What you'll bring**
---------------------

* Meaningful senior operational tenure in residential homebuilding — COO, Division President, VP Operations, or equivalent
* Demonstrated track record in high\-volume production environments; experience at 1,000\+ homes per year strongly preferred
* Deep, hands\-on background in land acquisition, entitlement, and development — not borrowed familiarity
* Finance and banking literacy tied to development: construction financing, lot banking, draw structures, and capital efficiency
* Experience in privately held, entrepreneurial companies preferred; comfort in lean, fast\-moving, low\-bureaucracy environments is a genuine advantage
* Data\-driven operator who starts the day with dashboards and ends it reviewing metrics

**Leadership profile**
----------------------


The right person for this role is assertive and high\-urgency, data\-driven and report\-reliant, disciplined in routine, willing to push back constructively, and equally willing to commit once a decision is made. They build people as well as processes, and they are as present in the field as they are behind a desk.

**Competencies**
----------------

* Results orientation
* Strategic thinking
* Leadership \& talent development
* Analytical thinking
* Collaboration \& influence
* Adaptability
* Integrity \& professionalism

----------------------


This is a field\-present, high\-visibility executive role based in Orlando, Florida. Regular travel between communities, divisional offices, and land sites is expected. new_jobs.title: General Psychiatry Residency Program Director - Psychiatrist
new_jobs.description:
**Description**


**MaineHealth Behavioral Health (MHBH)** is seeking a full\-time (1\.0 FTE) board\-certified Psychiatrist to join the Department of Psychiatry at MaineHealth Maine Medical Center Portland (MHMMCP). This role offers a unique hybrid opportunity, combining leadership and clinical practice.


The selected candidate will serve as the **General Psychiatry Residency Program Director** (0\.5 FTE) while also providing psychiatric clinical care (0\.5 FTE). This position supports a diverse patient population across both rural and urban communities.


This is an excellent opportunity for a psychiatrist interested in academic leadership, with potential for future involvement in additional academic and/or administrative roles.


The MHMMC General Psychiatry residency program combines the intellectual and physical resources of an academic teaching hospital with the patient base and public health commitment of a large community hospital and community mental health center. In addition to the General Adult Psychiatry Training Track, our residency program offers a General Psychiatry/Child \& Adolescent Psychiatry Integrated Training Track, as well as a Rural Psychiatry Training Track. Our care continuum and psychiatry residency training sites also include MaineHealth Behavioral Health at Spring Harbor (a free\-standing 100\-bed psychiatric hospital) and MaineHealth Behavioral Health, a region\-wide comprehensive mental health organization. MHMMCP also includes the Barbara Bush Children’s Hospital, the state’s only pediatric tertiary care center and only Level 1 Trauma Center.


MHMMC has an academic affiliation with Tufts University School of Medicine and offers the best aspects of patient care and academic stimulation. Residents are involved in teaching medical students from Tufts and from the nearby University of New England. Residents are also actively involved in department governance and decision\-making, participating in department retreats and quality improvement projects, and having formal representation on departmental committees.


We are very interested in furthering the practice of psychiatry in New England \- particularly in Maine. We have special options for rural psychiatry rotations while offering community\-based training experiences in Portland. We are proud of our program and take great pleasure in the success of our graduating residents.


MHMMC is a nationally recognized academic medical center with an impressive history of outstanding and innovative residency and fellowship programs. MHMMC is approved to train over 400 trainees in our 17 ACGME\-accredited residency programs, 19 ACGME\-accredited fellowship programs, two rural tracks and rural concentration. new_jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement
new_jobs.description:
**POSITION: Director of Community Engagement and Academy Giving**

**LOCATION: Great Hearts Irving Lower and Upper Schools; Irving, Texas**

**DIRECTLY REPORTS TO: Headmasters of Great Hearts Irving**

**FUNCTIONAL REPORTING TO: GHTX Development**

**SALARY: $50,000\-59,000**

* Occasional travel within Texas may be required.

**About Great Hearts Texas:**


Great Hearts Texas is a network of tuition\-free public schools dedicated to improving education in Texas. A Great Hearts Texas Academy cultivates great\-hearted leaders capable of success throughout their higher education and professional careers. With a curriculum built upon a classical liberal arts tradition and a revolutionary approach to education, Great Hearts Texas nurtures the hearts and minds of students in the pursuit of Truth, Goodness, and Beauty.

**Purpose:**


This role sits at the intersection of development and community relations. The Director of Community Engagement and Academy Giving (DCE) advances the academy’s mission by securing financial support through the annual Community Investment campaign and other giving opportunities, expanding outreach when necessary, and strengthening community ties. Reporting to the campus Headmaster, with functional support from GHTX Development as well as Marketing and Enrollment teams, the DCE plans and executes annual Community Investment campaigns, cultivates donor relationships, and fosters partnerships to boost student enrollment and enhance the academy’s reputation. This role requires strong communication, relationship\-building, and organizational skills. The DCE regularly collaborates with faculty, parents, volunteers, and the broader community to align fundraising priorities with the academy’s mission and effectively expand the academy’s brand and outreach.

**Responsibilities:**

**Fundraising and Development:**

* Lead the planning and execution of the Community Investment campaign in alignment with GHTX strategies to meet and exceed goals.
* Cultivate, solicit, and steward relationships with academy families, faculty, alumni, and community stakeholders to secure financial support.
* Identify and cultivate matching gifts, partnerships, and small grant opportunities toward the Community Investment fund and other fundraising initiatives.
* Using approved platforms, maintain standard operating procedures for gift entry and constituent data records.
* Maintain Community Investment visibility at events, meetings, and other vital channels to foster a culture of philanthropy.
* Report on key metrics and trends to the academy headmasters.
* Attend regular meetings with other Directors of Community Engagement and Academy Giving and central office support teams.

**Community Engagement and Outreach:**

* Advance outreach and marketing impact through strategic efforts to increase brand awareness and enrollment demand according to the academy’s goals.
* Drive initiatives to build strong partnerships by assisting the administration in hosting events, family tours, and other programming.
* Manage or support campus communication channels as needed (email, social, website, etc).
* Serve as a key partner to the academy’s Academy Advisory Committee (AAC) and Parent Service Organization (PSO).
* Represent the academy at internal and external functions, maintaining a positive public image.
* Collaborate with GHTX Marketing and Enrollment teams to promote growth and re\-enrollment.

**Qualifications:**

**Education:** A Bachelor's Degree

**Experience:** Minimum of 2–3 years of successful experience in fundraising, sales, marketing, or a related field.

**Skills:**

* Excellent oral and written communication skills, including presentation and storytelling abilities.
* Strong interpersonal skills with an outgoing, relationship\-oriented personality.
* Proven ability to take initiative, prioritize tasks, and work independently while collaborating effectively with a team.
* Proficiency in data analysis and reporting to inform strategic decisions.
* Experience in enrollment marketing and community outreach is highly desirable.
* Commitment to Great Hearts Texas's mission and classical education principles.
* Fluency in Spanish is an asset.
* Certified Fund\-Raising Executive (CFRE) designation is an asset.

**Computer Skills:**

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).
* Familiarity with Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Slides).
* Experience with constituent databases and giving platforms; familiarity with Raiser's Edge and Classy is beneficial.
* Skilled in utilizing email marketing tools and managing social media outlets.

**Travel Requirements:**


May need to travel locally to meet with academy families, attend school activities, and participate in community events.

**Physical Requirements:**


Ability to perform tasks involving standing, sitting, bending, squatting, reaching, and occasional lifting of up to 15 pounds.


It may require moving or positioning equipment for events and activities.

**Additional Information:**


Must pass a mandatory background screening.


Expected to follow the campus administrative schedule, including participation in summer and winter activities as required.


Serve as a visible and active presence on campus, aligning with the culture and values of Great Hearts Texas.

**Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a criminal history background check and fingerprint clearance in accordance with state requirements.**

**Travel required: May need to travel locally for training and professional development opportunities.**

**This description reflects management’s assignment of essential functions. It does not exclude or restrict the tasks that may be assigned.**

**Great Hearts Academies is an Equal Opportunity Employer.**

**Requisition Number** FE04968

* An earned doctorate in Social Work from an accredited institution
* An earned Master of Social Work degree from a CSWE\-accredited program


  

**Required Related Experience**
A record of teaching, scholarship, and service commensurate with appointment at the rank of Associate Professor or Professor with tenure. Strong potential for securing external funding and producing high\-quality scholarship. Ability to foster, develop, and/or maintain positive professional relationships with local, state, federal, and private social work focused agencies/organizations/associations.
  

**Required License/Registration/Certification**
n/a
  

**Job Summary**
THE UNIVERSITY OF KENTUCKY, COLLEGE OF SOCIAL WORK (CoSW) is a renowned leader in higher education. Our mission is clear: Through rigorous research, excellence in instruction, and steadfast service, the CoSW works to improve the human condition. Always, in all ways.  

As the state’s flagship university, CoSW is committed to actualizing our mission through innovative, accessible academic programming. CoSW is home to several undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral programs, including: Bachelor of Arts in Criminal Justice (traditional and online), Bachelor of Science in Criminal Justice (traditional and online), Bachelor of Arts in Social Work (traditional and online), Master of Science in Criminal Justice (online), Master of Social Work (hybrid and online), Doctorate of Social Work (online), Ph.D. in Social Work (traditional), and multiple certificate programs. In addition to Lexington’s main campus, we have a satellite campus at Fort Sam Houston in San Antonio, Texas.  

The Chair and Executive Director of Social Work Programs serves as the chief academic and administrative leader for the College’s social work educational enterprise. The Chair provides visionary leadership and strategic oversight for all aspects of the College’s social work programs, including the Bachelor of Arts in Social Work, Master of Social Work, Doctorate of Social Work, Doctor of Philosophy in Social Work, and related certificate programs.  

Reporting directly to the Dean and serving as a member of the College leadership team, the Chair and Executive Director advances the College’s strategic vision through academic leadership, faculty development, student success, community engagement, operational excellence, and organizational growth.  

Primary responsibilities of this position include but are not limited to:  

**Leads Strategic Growth and Innovation*** Develops and implements the strategic vision for the College’s social work programs.
* Guides academic innovation and program growth across modalities.
* Uses workforce, enrollment, and market data to inform planning.
* Identifies opportunities for new educational initiatives.

**Advances Faculty Success*** Recruits, mentors, supervises, and evaluates faculty and instructional personnel.
* Supports promotion, tenure, annual review, and workload planning.
* Supports faculty leadership development.
* Cultivates a collaborative faculty culture.

**Promotes Academic Excellence*** Oversees BASW, MSW, DSW, PhD, and certificate programs.
* Supports curriculum innovation.
* Ensures compliance with CSWE and SACSCOC.
* Promotes instructional quality across all modalities.

**Supports Student Success*** Partners with admissions, advising, practicum, recruitment, and student success.
* Advances recruitment, retention, persistence, and graduation initiatives.

**Strengthens Community Impact*** Develops relationships with agencies, alumni, professional organizations, and community partners.
* Supports fundraising and workforce partnerships.
* Expands community\-engaged scholarship and education.

**Manages Resources for Organizational Success*** Oversees personnel, budgeting, operational planning, and resource allocation.
* Collaborates with College leadership to advance strategic priorities.

The University’s mission involves three primary functions across our faculty cohort: instruction, research, and service. Each year, various ranking faculty work with the Office of the Dean to delineate their distribution of effort (DOE). This DOE outlines how faculty will spend their time. In general, DOE for faculty members in the Regular Title Series typically includes allocations in the areas of instruction, research, and service. The DOE for the Chair and Executive Director is subject to negotiation but we anticipate roughly 70% Administration, 25% research and 5% service.
  

  

Of course, the DOE can fluctuate depending on an array of factors (e.g., grant funding, new course development, service to the college, etc.). It is expected that work in this faculty appointment, including but not limited to course instruction, office hours, administrative meetings, and attending college\-wide events such as faculty meetings, will occur on\-site.  

  

Employment at UK is subject to fund availability and comes with many rewards, focusing on your total well\-being and career development, with leadership striving to provide a strong work\-life integration. The university generously contributes to employees’ retirement plans, medical coverage, and life insurance. In addition, UK offers optional benefits such as dental and vision insurance, additional retirement plans and much more. To learn more about these benefits, please visit: **https://hr.uky.edu/employment/our\-benefits**.

new_jobs.title: Director of Operations
new_jobs.description:
**Director Of Operations**

*Our mantra is simple \- love. Love what you do. Love where you live. Love the success and return we provide. At RR Living, we are a part of something special.*


The Director of Operations is a key leadership position responsible for growing a team of people who will effectively execute the company’s business strategy. Operational leaders are empowered to drive the financial success of multi\-million\-dollar communities and assets within a defined portfolio/region while providing strategic leadership, management oversight and accountability for several areas of performance including property operations, portfolio financial results, compliance, talent acquisition, team member development, customer and resident satisfaction, asset preservation, service, facilities \& expense control. You ensure that established business strategy and financial performance targets are achieved or exceeded.


**Responsibilities**

* You and your community teams are expected to drive operational improvement including increasing physical and economic occupancy at the communities assigned to you. This will be accomplished through hiring and developing a stable well\-trained team of professionals who understand the RR Living Core Values and drive excellence at the community and with resident satisfaction.
* You are expected to achieve Budgeted Income, Expenses and CNOI every month, quarter, and year on the assets you are responsible for.
* Proactively recognize trends and market conditions that may impact property performance. Become an expert on the markets you are in, know your competition and how those communities align with our community.
* Using strategy and experience, successfully lead through economic downturns to ensure the assets under your direction are leading the market in performance and proforma budget achievement.
* Achieve and maintain delinquency at less than 2% on stabilized assets. On assigned assets above 2%, goal percentages will be developed during your first 30 days of employment, to outline tiered expectations to ultimately achieve the 2% or better goal on each asset within 90 days.
* Achieve portfolio and proforma occupancy goals and maintaining a 95% or above occupancy
* Grow rental rate and income in accordance with ownership business strategies and assigned budget, and at a minimum striving to achieve 2% more than market average.
* Build a team of direct reports and community team members that understand the importance of executing an exemplary resident experience, receiving excellent and respectful service every day.
* Ensure your portfolio pays attention to the details, including curb appeal, a safe and enjoyable community atmosphere, well maintained amenities, and rental homes where residents are proud to have family and friends visit.
* Ensure communities are well\-maintained physically, including make\-readies, preventive maintenance, and the completion of service requests within 48 hours of submission.
* Ensure communities in your portfolio achieve net move\-in goals, retention and rate expectations and administrative reporting that is on time and accurate.
* Hire, train, mentor and develop future leaders and community team members. Proactively manage underperformers by training them, developing them and respectfully off boarding those who are not performing.
* Frequently conduct physical property walks, including the inspection of all grounds, community spaces such as hallways, breezeways, vacant apartment homes, clubhouses, shops, amenity areas, entrance and exit areas and community offices to ensure cleanliness, condition and that all areas are in good working order.
* Quickly learn how to navigate and use the computer software programs utilized by the company including Real Page One Site, On\-Site, AppFolio, Knock, Buzz, Apartment IQ Rentable, and more.
* Maintain ethical, professional, respectful, and courteous relationships with residents, teammates, and other customers. Follow all local, federal, and state regulations including Fair Housing Guidelines
* Act as an Ambassador of RR Living building relationships in the surrounding neighborhoods and community, and in our RR Giving Impact Initiatives.
* Ask questions, think strategically and lead your team with a Founder’s Mentality while being an integral and key part of the property management leadership team.

**RR Living's Core Values**

* **Be Your Best. Do Your Best.**

*We celebrate individualism, collaboration, and inclusion. Our associates are the best in the business, exemplifying that which we celebrate as an organization. Recognizing happiness and great attitudes are contagious, we hold ourselves and each other accountable. Success begets success and happiness begets happiness***.**




* **Honesty, Integrity, and an Unwavering Commitment to Excellence:**

*Excellent resident experiences are our specialty, recognizing the unique challenges of rentership. We provide a wonderful place to call Home, striving to do what is often missed \- creating unparalleled living experiences for our residents, incredible opportunities for our associates, and impressive revenues for our partners \&; owners.* ***Simply put, we Care.***




* **Empowered Associates, Obsessively Purpose\-Driven and Stronger Together:**

*Success, a people\-centric approach, and revenue growth are not independent of each other. We operate as one team. deliberate in the actions taken to drive revenue and improved valuation for owners \& investors. As happy performers, our associates are an engaged team empowered to work together to achieve our common goals, making us an unstoppable successful organization***.**




* **The Magic is in the Details:**

*Recognizing that residents choose to live where they can be proud of residing, we understand that details matter. Our teams provide personalized service that exceeds expectations and creates unique neighborhood\-like environments. From elite resident events to local partnerships

new_jobs.description:
**POSITION TITLE:** Senior Director of Development

 **CLASSIFICATION:** Exempt

 **STATUS:** Full\-Time

 **DEPARTMENT:** Advancement

 **REPORTS TO:** Vice President of Advancement

 **SUPERVISES:** N/A

 **POSITION SUMMARY*****:***


Kentucky Wesleyan College seeks a collaborative, strategic, and relationship\-driven fundraising professional to serve as Senior Director of Development. This leadership position is responsible for expanding philanthropic support through the identification, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship of major and planned gift donors.


The Senior Director manages a portfolio of approximately 100–150 major gift prospects and donors, developing personalized engagement strategies that inspire transformational philanthropy. Working in partnership with Advancement colleagues, academic leadership, faculty, alumni, volunteers, and community stakeholders, this position advances the College's mission by securing significant philanthropic investments that support institutional priorities and student success.


The successful candidate is an experienced frontline fundraiser who combines strong relationship\-building skills with strategic planning, data\-informed decision\-making, and a commitment to exceptional donor experiences. This position contributes to a culture of philanthropy through collaboration, innovation, accountability, and measurable fundraising outcomes.

 **PRIMARY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Develop and execute strategies to identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward major and planned gift prospects in support of Kentucky Wesleyan College's mission and strategic priorities.
* Manage a portfolio of approximately 100\-150 major gift prospects and donors, with a focus on donor retention, upgrades, long\-term engagement, and gifts of significant philanthropic impact.
* Conduct regular discovery, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship visits with alumni, friends, parents, and community partners, utilizing data\-informed moves management practices.
* Develop individualized donor engagement and solicitation strategies that align donor interests with institutional funding priorities and increase philanthropic support.
* Build and maintain a healthy major gift pipeline through prospect research, qualification, tracking, forecasting, and collaboration with Advancement colleagues.
* Partner with faculty, staff, and campus leaders to create meaningful donor engagement opportunities and strengthen relationships across the College community.
* Lead and support donor stewardship and recognition efforts, ensuring donors are meaningfully engaged, acknowledged, and informed about the impact of their philanthropy.
* Collaborate with Advancement colleagues to develop compelling donor communications, promote institutional impact, and share alumni, student, and donor success stories.
* Assist in the planning and execution of donor cultivation, stewardship, recognition, and advancement events.
* Maintain accurate donor records, contact reports, and prospect activity within the College's constituent relationship management system.
* Serve as a strategic partner to Advancement leadership by contributing to fundraising strategy, revenue growth initiatives, and best practices in donor engagement.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the Vice President for Advancement.

 **REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:**


Bachelor’s degree; minimum of two years of experience in major gift fundraising preferably in an educational environment; a proven and verifiable track record of success in identifying, cultivating, and soliciting major gifts.

 **REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:**

* Clear understanding of moves management in professional fundraising.
* Proven ability to successfully identify and build relationships with donors to connect their interests with opportunities in a higher education or other nonprofit organization.
* Basic understanding of planned gift concepts.
* A demonstrated ability to engage and effectively communicate with diverse audiences.
* Excellent oral, written, and interpersonal communication skills, including the ability to persuasively articulate institutional impact and funding needs.
* Strong work ethic, self\-awareness, and ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with colleagues across campus.
* Ability and willingness to travel, work occasional evenings and weekends, and participate in donor and institutional events as needed.
* Valid driver's license or ability to obtain reliable transportation for travel related to fundraising and constituent engagement activities.

 **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Ability to develop and execute fundraising plans with strong support of metrics.
* High level of creativity, initiative, and motivation.
* Demonstrated knowledge of all facets of fundraising, including annual fund, corporate and foundation relations, planned giving, stewardship, major gift fundraising, etc.
* Ability to work cross\-functionally with academic and administrative leaders in a collaborative environment to conceive and implement innovative ideas.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and experience working in a CRM or other relational database such as Blackbaud Raiser’s Edge.
* Knowledge of best practices in alumni engagement, board and volunteer cultivation and development, project implementation and evaluation.

**WORK HOURS/CONDITIONS:**


Office environment; 40 hours per week; normally 8:00 a.m.\-5:00 p.m.; some evening and weekend work required.

new_jobs.title: Director of Marketing and Communications
new_jobs.description:
JGA’s clients are achieving important successes across the nation in Education, Healthcare, the Arts, and Human Services, and we empower and accelerate generosity in support of their work.

Johnson, Grossnickle and Associates (JGA) is a philanthropic consulting firm that is **employee\-owned.** Our members are a collaborative team of experienced professionals with deep expertise committed to innovation in the nonprofit sector. We partner with clients on fundraising strategies to advance their philanthropic goals.

We are growing and are currently seeking a **Director of Marketing and Communications** to join our team.

The Director of Marketing and Communications leads JGA’s efforts to effectively drive a strategic marketing approach ensuring close alignment with the sales enablement strategy. Thie Director leads and implements marketing and communication for JGA and reports to a Senior Consultant.

The successful candidate will work effectively within a team\-oriented and mission\-driven environment. Strategy, strong communication, and self\-motivation are crucial to success. JGA takes a thoughtful approach to philanthropic consulting and acts as a guide in philanthropy; we are authentic counselors to our diverse clientele, and this position will help reflect this externally.

This is a full\-time, hybrid position, with expected travel to the office at least 3 days a week to attend in\-person meetings in our office just south of Indianapolis in Greenwood, Indiana.

**Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Lead JGA’s marketing efforts that support the goals of the JGA strategic plan, build our national presence in the nonprofit sector, and accelerate our growing strategic partnerships.
* Implement strategy on marketing, communications, and brand presence ensuring it aligns with the firm’s overall sales enablement efforts. This includes conferences, JGA hosted in\-person events, webinars, blogs, and social media.
* Coordinate content development, daily marketing outreach, and website and social media presence, in close partnership with the Director of Business Development.
* Strategize with JGA consultants regarding thought leadership blogs, speaking opportunities, publications, and cross\-industry collaborations.
* Monitor the effectiveness of core marketing channels and shift resources to maximize return on investment.

**Preferred qualifications include:**

* Strategic leader who can learn quickly, communicate well, and proactively generate ideas and solutions.
* Passion for philanthropy, for accelerating the missions of nonprofits and the good they do in the world.
* An action\-focused team player who is energized by meeting goals creatively and collaboratively.
* Excellent organizational skills (oral and written) and the ability to excel at details, multitasking, and working under pressure.
* Engaged and positive teamworking capability with everyone at JGA.
* Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, or related field.
* Familiarity with constituent CRMs, web content management, and email communication platforms. (HubSpot, WordPress, Microsoft, and Adobe products).
* Five or more years of marketing experience with a variety of marketing channels (web, digital, social media, email, and print.)
* Experience across various marketing functions including brand identity, demand generation, sales pipeline, thought leadership, and events.

**Physical requirements:**

* Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer and talking on the phone.
* Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.

**JGA’s Commitment to Diversity:**

**We are committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion.** We work to advance equity, access, and inclusion of diverse people and perspectives in our work as a team, with our clients, in the philanthropic sector, and in the community.

Guided by our JGA values, we are authentically engaged in this work and monitoring, reflecting on, and adjusting our approaches when needed. We are focused on:

* continuing to diversify our team;
* strengthening our DEI competencies in our work with clients; and
* Ensuring our partnerships and work in the community, meaningfully reflect and advance our DEI priorities.

**Compensation, Benefits, and Perks**

* Competitive salary based on experience
* Medical/dental/vision options for employee and dependents
* Voluntary benefit options
* Employee Assistance Plan (EAP)
* Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP)
* 401(k)
* Generous PTO plan that increases with tenure

* Hybrid working options
* Individualized onboarding plan

*This job description is an overview of the primary responsibilities and qualifications for this position. We value agility, flexibility, and growth potential, so this job description is not inclusive of all duties you might be asked to perform or of all qualifications that may be required either now or in the future.*

Pay: $80,000\.00 \- $95,000\.00 per year
